units.title: product-ui.md scope: applications are used, not visited
units.summary: New reference read whenever Phase 0 classifies the surface as an application (logged-in product, admin, dashboard, console) or a hybrid (sign-in, onboarding, docs, configurator). Frames the whole file: everything else in the skill was written for marketing pages judged by strangers in seconds; an application is the same people for hours every day doing the same tasks, so 'the identity carries over; the expression does not.'
units.quote: An application is the opposite case: the same people spend hours in it, every day, doing the same tasks. The identity carries over; the expression does not.
units.whereInMine: references/app-ui.md header: 'Read in Phases 3–5 whenever a route is a productive surface (framing.md). A marketing page is judged in five seconds; a product screen is judged over hundreds of uses.'
units.conflict: Vocabulary: branch says 'application' / 'marketing (visited)'; 2.0 says productive vs expressive posture per route. Do not add a second product-UI file.
units.destination: references/app-ui.md (header paragraph) — keep 2.0's file; fold the 'identity carries over, expression does not' line into P1-02's destination
units.notes: 2.0's app-ui.md already plays this role. Only the one-line thesis is new, and P1-02 handles it.

units.title: Carry the brand's identity into the product, not its expression
units.summary: Carry into the product: the mark, the colours and their meanings, the voice of the display face, and the status vocabulary. Leave on the marketing site: display scale, editorial pacing, persuasive copy, photography and decorative motion.
units.quote: Carry the brand's identity into the product — mark, colours and their meanings, the voice of the display face, the status vocabulary. Leave its expression — display scale, editorial pacing, persuasive copy, photography, decorative motion — on the marketing site.
units.whereInMine: art-direction.md §6 'Where brand shows — type, colour roles, empty states, onboarding, success moments, marketing-to-product seams'; §5 'brand layer only — type, colour roles, marks, tone'; categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories': 'Never let marketing type, motion or gradients leak into the app'; categories.md SaaS 'Do not import from marketing: big hero type, scroll reveals, hover lifts, gradients and glow, testimonial energy, illustration in the chrome.'
units.conflict: Terminology: 2.0 calls the transferable part the 'brand layer' and uses 'expressive' as a posture name. 'Expression' as a noun for the non-transferable devices could be confused with the expressive posture, so phrase it as 'the brand layer carries over; expressive devices do not'. 2.0 lacks two items: 'colours and their meanings' (which hue is action, live, ground) and 'status vocabulary'.
units.destination: references/app-ui.md §1 Principles (new principle 0 or 8: 'The brand layer carries over; the site's expressive devices do not'), cross-referenced from art-direction.md §6 'Where brand shows'
units.notes: This is the branch's central idea. The quote-block formulation is sharper than anything in 2.0. Keep 2.0's 'brand layer' term and add colour meanings and status vocabulary to its definition.

units.title: Evidence: Carbon productive/expressive sets and Material 3 role split
units.summary: Carbon has two type sets. The productive set is 'for product pages with high information density housed in containers', on a 14 px base with fixed headings. The expressive set is for web pages, on a 16 px base with fluid headings. Carbon warns against fluid styles inside a container. Material 3 splits its scale into display/headline roles for expressive moments and title/body/label roles for the interface.
units.quote: Material 3 splits its scale into display and headline roles for expressive moments and title, body and label roles for the interface.
units.whereInMine: design-systems.md §3 'Productive (product UI): 14 px base (13 in dense tools), fixed sizes… Carbon: "fixed type styles are a must"'; 'Expressive… Carbon: "Do not use these styles inside a container"'; design-theory.md C2 'Two sets on one system'. Material's role split is absent.
units.destination: references/design-systems.md §3 Type sets per surface (add the Material 3 display/headline vs title/body/label split as a second source)
units.notes: Carbon is fully covered. Only the Material 3 role mapping is new.

units.title: Classify the surface: visited vs used signal table
units.summary: A table of nine signals separating marketing (visited) from application (used). Who: strangers once or twice vs the same people daily. Session: seconds to minutes scrolling vs minutes to hours, task after task. Success: remembered/persuaded/converted vs task done fast, correctly, without strain. Reading mode: glancing then story vs scanning, comparing, entering data. Density: one idea per viewport vs as high as comprehension allows. Navigation: a few pages in a linear story vs many tools jumped between. Copy: persuasive vs labels of 2–4 words. Motion: can carry the concept vs feedback and live state only. Imagery: photography can carry the concept vs almost none. Also the rationale: treating an app like a landing page 'fails its users slowly' (every screen costs a scroll, every visit replays an entrance).
units.quote: A redesign that treats an application like a landing page fails its users slowly: every screen costs a scroll, every label is a little harder to read, every visit replays an entrance nobody needs.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1 category/posture table and per-route frequency/stakes; framing.md §2 'What the classification switches on or off' (motion, novelty, density, success measures); framing.md §3 'appropriate first; attractive-but-inappropriate is the characteristic failure'.
units.conflict: 2.0 classifies into 11 categories with four postures, not a two-way split. The table must feed the category/posture choice and not replace it.
units.destination: references/framing.md §1 Classify every route (add the signals as a 'how to tell visited from used' aid before the category table)
units.notes: The Reading mode, Navigation and Imagery rows have no 2.0 counterpart. The 'fails slowly' rationale can be one sentence under framing §3.

units.title: Application copy: labels, states, instructions of 2–4 words (NN/g)
units.summary: In an application, copy is labels, states and instructions of 2–4 words (NN/g UI copy), not persuasive or memorable marketing copy.
units.quote: labels, states, instructions, 2–4 words (NN/g)
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §1.7 'Content is design. Labels in the users' words; one name per thing… product UI written as product UI, not as marketing'; app-ui.md §5 'column titles of one or two words'; critique.md #21.
units.destination: references/app-ui.md §1 principle 7 'Content is design' (add the 2–4 word label norm with the NN/g source)
units.notes: Only the numeric norm is new.

units.title: Family test between the marketing site and the product
units.summary: When the product has a marketing site, test the product against that site's identity, not its layout. In an application redesign this 'family test' replaces the distance test's hero and rhythm items. A user who moves from the marketing site into the product should recognise the house (mark, colour, voice) and immediately find the product calmer, denser and faster than the site.
units.quote: The family test replaces the distance test's hero and rhythm items: a user moving from the marketing site into the product should recognise the house (mark, colour, voice) and immediately find the product calmer, denser and faster than the site.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md 'Distance, used where it belongs' turns the distance test off on productive surfaces; art-direction.md §5 runs convergence checks on the brand layer only for productive routes; categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories' ('Share the truth… Never let marketing type… leak into the app'). There is no positive test for the marketing-to-product seam.
units.conflict: Name clash: 2.0 already uses 'family test' in logo-design.md 6b (the mark beside parent and sibling marks) and in lessons.md. Rename this one, for example 'seam test' or 'same-house test'. Also 2.0 does not replace the distance test on productive routes; it switches it off.
units.destination: references/art-direction.md §5 Convergence checks (a productive-route bullet: the seam test), and §6 'Where brand shows'
units.notes: This gives productive routes a positive brand check to go with the brand-layer convergence tests. Keep the three observable outcomes: recognised house, calmer, denser/faster.

units.title: Hybrids: doors, reading surfaces and tools
units.summary: Hybrids follow the rule of their job. Sign-in, empty states and onboarding are 'doors': one brand moment, then out of the way. Docs are reading surfaces (body 16 px, measure 60–75 ch). A pricing calculator inside the app is a tool.
units.quote: Hybrids get the rule of their job: sign-in, empty states and onboarding are doors — one brand moment, then out of the way.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1 'Classify per route or route group, not per repo'; categories.md Dev tools and docs 'prose 15–16 px at 60–75 characters'; art-direction.md §6 lists onboarding and empty states as places brand shows. The 'door' concept is absent.
units.destination: references/framing.md §1 (a hybrid rule under the category table) and references/categories.md (docs numbers already present)
units.notes: The docs numbers are already in 2.0. The new parts are the 'door' framing for sign-in, onboarding and empty states, and calling a calculator inside an app a tool.

units.title: Productive type roles with Carbon and Material 3 numbers
units.summary: Role table from Carbon packages/type/src/styles.ts and Material md-sys-typescale tokens. Label/caption: label-01 12/16; M3 label-medium 12/16, label-small 11/16. Body dense: body-compact-01 14/18; body-medium 14/20 (table cells, rows, controls). Body reading: body-01 14/20, body-02 16/24; body-large 16/24. Small heading: heading-compact-01 14/18 semibold, -02 16/22; title-small 14/20, title-medium 16/24 (500) for panel, card and table group titles. Section heading: heading-03 20/28; title-large 22/28. Page title: heading-04 28/36, heading-05 32/40; headline-small 24/32, -medium 28/36, one per screen. Display: expressive only (fluid, up to 60 px+) or display 36–57, not in the product (sign-in at most).
units.quote: Numbers from the systems' source files (Carbon packages/type/src/styles.ts, Material md-sys-typescale tokens)
units.whereInMine: design-systems.md §3 lists the productive role names (heading, title, body, label, detail, metric, code) and the 14 px base. categories.md 'Measured reference points: … Carbon productive set 14 px fixed vs expressive 16 px fluid'. SYSTEM.md Type line. No per-role sizes or line heights.
units.conflict: 2.0's role list includes 'code'. See P1-16 on monospace.
units.destination: references/design-systems.md §3 Type sets per surface (a role table), referenced from templates/SYSTEM.md 'Type' and app-ui.md §3
units.notes: This is the most concrete new table in the branch. Keep the source-file citations.

units.title: 12 px floor for readable text; 11 px only for one uppercase word
units.summary: Nothing a user must read goes below 12 px. 11 px is allowed only for a single uppercase word.
units.quote: 12 px is the floor; 11 px only for a single uppercase word
units.whereInMine: dataviz.md 'chart text ≥ 12 px' covers charts only. categories.md cites 'Apple iOS body 17 pt (minimum 11)'. No general UI text floor.
units.destination: references/app-ui.md §3 Density and layout (type floor), and design-systems.md §3
units.notes: This is also a candidate audit.mjs --kind app signal (text below 12 px), which would be a script unit for the scripts group.

units.title: Base 14/20; reading text 15–16 px
units.summary: Product UI base is 14 px with a 20 px line height. Text read in sentences (descriptions, notes) is 15–16 px.
units.quote: Base 14 px, line height 20; reading text 15–16 px.
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §3 'Body 13–14 px'; design-systems.md §3 '14 px base (13 in dense tools)'; categories.md SaaS '13–14 px body'. No line height and no reading-text size inside apps.

units.title: 4.5:1 on every ground text sits on, including hover, zebra, secondary panels and selected
units.summary: Text needs at least 4.5:1 on every surface it sits on. That includes hover rows, zebra stripes, secondary panels and selected states, not only the base surface.
units.quote: Minimum 4.5:1 on every surface the text sits on — including hover rows, zebra stripes, secondary panels and selected states

units.title: Fixed headings: page titles 24–32 px; no marketing display sizes
units.summary: Headings in the product are fixed, not fluid. Page titles are 24–32 px. The marketing site's 60–120 px display sizes never enter the product.
units.quote: Fixed headings. Page titles 24–32 px. The marketing site's 60–120 px display sizes never enter the product.

units.title: The brand display face gets one job in the product
units.summary: The brand's display face gets one job, typically the page title (and the sign-in or greeting moment). Panel titles, record names in lists, numbers and labels use the UI face, where weight does the work: 500–600 at 14–16 px scans faster than a serif at 20 px.
units.quote: The brand's display face gets one job, typically the page title (and the sign-in / greeting moment).
units.whereInMine: art-direction.md §6 'Where brand shows — type, colour roles…'; design-systems.md §3 'Weight is hierarchy'; anti-patterns.md App-UI tells 'a greeting — "Welcome back, Alex 👋" — in the title slot, where the title should name the place and scope'.
units.conflict: 2.0 lists a greeting in the title slot as a generated-dashboard tell. The branch names the greeting as the display face's job and as a brand moment. Resolve by keeping the greeting out of the page-title slot, or by allowing one only on a home screen whose title still names the place.
units.destination: references/app-ui.md §3 (type) and art-direction.md §6 'Where brand shows'
units.notes: 'One job for the display face' and 'serif record names and KPI numerals are wrong' are new in 2.0 and worth keeping. Only the greeting clause conflicts.

units.title: Numbers: tabular lining figures in the UI face; KPI numerals 24–32 px semibold
units.summary: Use tabular lining figures in the UI face, right-aligned in tables. KPI numerals are 24–32 px semibold, not a decorative display cut.
units.quote: KPI numerals 24–32 px, semibold — not a decorative display cut.

units.title: Caps in apps: only one or two words in isolation, 11–12 px, 0.04–0.06 em
units.summary: NN/g's glanceable-type study found uppercase faster for a word or two in isolation. So short column heads and one-word nav group labels may be uppercase at 11–12 px with 0.04–0.06 em tracking. Multi-word strings, statuses read in sequence, window bars with sentences in them, and anything scanned down a column stay sentence case.
units.quote: NN/g's glanceable-type study found uppercase faster for a word or two in isolation
units.whereInMine: design-theory.md C1 'letterspace all strings of capitals and small caps by 5–12%'; C3 'tracked small capitals in a hard grotesk at 10–13px read as a spec sheet or code… allow at most one small-caps device on the page'; anti-patterns.md purpose-gated 'Tracked small capitals as a label system | one device per page'.
units.conflict: The tracking values differ: the branch's 0.04 em is below 2.0's 5% minimum. The branch also allows two caps uses (column heads and nav group labels) where 2.0 allows one small-caps device per page, and 2.0's 10–13 px tracked-caps tell overlaps the branch's 11–12 px allowance.
units.destination: references/design-theory.md C1/C3 and app-ui.md §3 (a product-UI caps rule that fits 'one device')
units.notes: Keep the NN/g evidence and the sentence-case list (statuses, column-scanned text). Pick one tracking range, and count 'column heads plus nav group labels' as one device or tighten the rule.

units.title: No monospace in the product unless users read code; values in the UI face
units.summary: No monospace at all unless the product's users read code. IDs, passwords, env names, placeholders and keyboard hints go in the UI face at weight 500 with tabular figures. Add a copy button where a value is copied.
units.quote: IDs, passwords, env names, placeholders and keyboard hints go in the UI face at 500 with tabular figures (add a copy button where a value is copied).

The branch, after a third user rejection (Brio3), forbids it for IDs, passwords, env names, placeholders and key hints unless the audience reads code. The 'code' role in the productive set also needs the same condition.

units.destination: references/app-ui.md §3 Density and layout; anti-patterns.md App-UI tells (make rows and controls explicit)

units.title: Checklist before implementation (app surfaces)
units.summary: Nine checks. (1) Surface classified; marketing site sampled for identity only. (2) Type roles as fixed sizes with line heights, base 14/20, minimum 12, display face assigned one job. (3) Every text/ground pair at 4.5:1 including hover, selected, zebra, secondary panels and dark mode; every input border, focus ring and switch track at 3:1. (4) Page-header height budget; first rows of the main object above the fold at 1280 × 800. (5) Density per surface. (6) Navigation: grouped sidebar, phone drawer, tab titles, palette or shortcuts. (7) State inventory: five interaction states per control, four content states per data region. (8) Brand-moment budget and sign-in treatment decided. (9) After building: a11y.mjs clean on every route × theme × phone width with overlays open, a keyboard walk of the top tasks, and the §9 traps checked by hand.
units.quote: After building: scripts/a11y.mjs clean on every route × theme × phone width with overlays open, a keyboard walk of the top tasks, and the §9 traps checked by hand.

units.destination: references/app-ui.md (closing checklist, like design-theory.md Part D) and templates/DESIGN.md 'Productive surfaces'

units.title: Commitment 4: no monospace unless the audience reads code
units.summary: A developer or infrastructure tool may use a monospace face. Every other company, site or app gets none: not for labels, data, IDs, passwords, env names, [placeholders], keyboard hints or timers. Use the text face at 500 with tabular figures. A sibling site that already uses mono does not make it transferable. The browser's default monospace for code/kbd/samp/pre counts too. scripts/a11y.mjs fails any page that renders monospace text. The owner has rejected code-like type on three projects.

units.destination: SKILL.md Commitments (as a clause of commitment 3, or a new commitment 5), with anti-patterns.md purpose-gated 'Monospace' row tightened

units.conflict: Direct conflict. 2.0 allows mono for 'true machine identifiers' on any product, while the branch bans it for IDs and values unless the audience reads code. Per lessons 2026-09-25 (Brio3), this exception is what let mono leak back in. 2.0's 'Allowed when' column should say that the product's users read code (developer or infrastructure tools), and 'true machine identifiers' should go.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md purpose-gated table, Monospace row. Allowed when: the product's users read code (developer or infrastructure tools, code samples). Otherwise: the UI face at 500 with `tabular-nums`, plus a copy button for copied values. Add a matching line to app-ui.md §5 Tables and lists or §6 Forms.
units.notes: The owner has said this three times and it is recorded as a user correction (lessons 2026-09-25, second Brio3 row, owned by the lessons.md group). The branch wording should win over 2.0's 'true machine identifiers'.

units.title: Keyboard hints (Ctrl K, Esc) are not set in monospace
units.summary: Shortcut hints shown in the UI, such as `Ctrl K` and `Esc` keycaps in a search field, menu or tooltip, go in the UI face, not in a code font. In Brio3 they rendered in mono even after the mono label system had been removed.
units.quote: `Ctrl K` hints
units.whereInMine: 2.0 encourages shortcuts but says nothing about their type: app-ui.md §4 ("Commands in a command palette (⌘K) that shows each command's shortcut"), §10 ("Tooltips on icon-only buttons show the name *and* the shortcut"), categories.md L32 and L65 ("⌘K search").
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md purpose-gated Monospace row, 'Otherwise' column (keyboard hints in the UI face). Also app-ui.md §4 Navigation (command palette) or §10 Feel (tooltips): 'shortcut hints in the UI face, not a mono keycap'.
units.notes: Since 2.0 pushes shortcuts and palettes harder than 1.x, the chance of mono keycaps sneaking in is higher. Pair this with P2-04, because `kbd` is the usual element used.

units.title: The browser's default monospace for code/kbd counts as choosing mono
units.summary: Even when no mono face is loaded, the browser's default styles for `code` and `kbd` (and, per the branch's SKILL.md and product-ui.md, `samp` and `pre`) render a code font. That still counts as a violation. The fix from the branch's product-ui.md: point the framework's mono token (such as Tailwind `font-mono`) and the `code`/`kbd`/`samp`/`pre` defaults at the UI face. The branch's a11y.mjs checks the computed font of every text element and fails on monospace unless `--allow-mono` is passed.
units.quote: the browser default for `code`/`kbd`, which nobody chose but still renders a code font
units.whereInMine: No 2.0 reference or script mentions code/kbd/samp/pre defaults or a stray `font-mono` class. 2.0 scripts (a11y.mjs, audit.mjs) do not check the rendered font for monospace. audit.mjs only reports saturated faces with a share of 10% or more, which would miss a browser-default monospace.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md purpose-gated Monospace row, or a Hard bans line: 'browser-default monospace on code/kbd/samp/pre counts'. implementation.md base CSS: `code, kbd, samp, pre { font-family: inherit }` and the mono token repointed, unless the audience reads code. Script feature in a11y.mjs or audit.mjs: computed-font monospace check with `--allow-mono`.
units.notes: The a11y.mjs computed-font check and its --allow-mono flag come from branch commit 012233c. That is a script-feature unit for the a11y.mjs group, to be ported onto the 2.0 Playwright/lib/env.mjs a11y.mjs. This unit covers only the anti-pattern wording.

units.title: New section: 'Marketing expression transplanted into a product' (identity right, ergonomics wrong)
units.summary: A new anti-pattern section for the hybrid case: an app is made to 'match the site' and carries over the marketing site's expression instead of just its identity. It 'photographs well and tires the people who use it all day'. The section has 8 symptoms (P2-06 to P2-15, all seen in one real redesign, Brio3) and a closing test (P2-16/P2-17). It cites `lessons.md` 2026-09-25 and `product-ui.md` §1–2.
units.quote: The failure of "make the app match the site": the identity is right, the ergonomics are wrong. It photographs well and tires the people who use it all day.
units.whereInMine: 2.0 has the ideas but not this named failure. anti-patterns.md 'App-UI tells' (L110–122) covers the generic generated-dashboard look (shadcn, KPI tiles, card soup), not the brand's own marketing expression leaking into its app. SKILL.md L61: "brand shows in type, colour roles, tone and a few considered moments, not in custom controls". art-direction.md §6: "Where brand shows — type, colour roles, empty states, onboarding, success moments, marketing-to-product seams". framing.md §1: the Twenty CRM example of 'one company, two philosophies'. categories.md L35: "Do not import from marketing: big hero type, scroll reveals, hover lifts, gradients and glow, testimonial energy, illustration in the chrome."
units.conflict: Vocabulary. The branch says 'identity carries over, expression does not' and 'product' or 'app'. 2.0 says 'brand layer' (type, colour roles, marks, tone) carries over, and it contrasts 'expressive' with 'productive' surfaces. The branch cites `product-ui.md` §1–2, which in 2.0 is `app-ui.md` (§1 Principles, §3 Density and layout). The cited lesson row (2026-09-25 Brio3) is not in the 2.0 lessons.md yet.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md: a new H2 'Marketing expression transplanted into a productive surface', directly after 'App-UI tells' (or an H3 inside it). Rewrite it as 'the brand layer carries over; the expressive layer does not'. Cross-link from app-ui.md §11 App-UI tells and art-direction.md §6 'Where brand shows'.
units.notes: This depends on the lessons.md group porting both 2026-09-25 Brio3 rows (they are user corrections, add-lesson-row) and on the product-ui.md group merging into app-ui.md, so the cross-references resolve. The section is the anti-patterns half of branch commit 9241608 (Phase 0 classify, product-ui.md, and so on).

units.title: Display-size page titles with eyebrow and lead on every product screen
units.summary: Failure: a 40 px serif page title with an eyebrow index above it and a two-line lead below. That is 180 px of header before the first row of data, on every page, read once and then scrolled past forever. The rule: product page titles are 24–32 px, fixed (not fluid), and sit in one band with the page's actions.
units.quote: Display-size page titles on every screen
units.whereInMine: anti-patterns.md L114 App-UI tells: "Marketing type in a work tool (30–48 px headings; a greeting ... in the title slot, where the title should name the place and scope)". app-ui.md §1.3: "13–14 px body, 20–28 px page titles". categories.md L11: SaaS 'Largest text 20–28 px'. design-theory.md C2: productive set 'fixed sizes'. audit.mjs L296 flags largest text ≥ 32 px in app views ('work tools rarely need more than 24–28px'). Not covered: the eyebrow + lead stack, the 180 px header budget, and 'in one band with the actions'.
units.conflict: Number conflict. The branch allows 24–32 px (from Carbon heading-04/05 28/36 and 32/40, and Material headline-small/medium 24/32 and 28/36). 2.0 says 20–28 px, and audit.mjs flags 32 px as too big. Pick one range and keep app-ui.md, categories.md and audit.mjs consistent. The branch cites `product-ui.md` §1–2, which is `app-ui.md` in 2.0.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md App-UI tells, first bullet ('Marketing type in a work tool'): add 'an eyebrow above and a lead below the title on every screen; a page header taller than ~100 px before the main object'. app-ui.md §3 Density and layout: 'title band = title + view actions in one row; header height budget'.
units.notes: Could become an audit.mjs --kind app signal: the header height above the first table/list/form row, or an eyebrow above the h1 in app views. The branch product-ui.md checklist has 'Page header height budget'.

units.title: The site's small-caps label device used as the product's label system
units.summary: Failure: 10–11 px tracked monospace capitals on window bars, table heads, status words and stat labels. Caps are glanceable for one word (NN/g 'Typography for Glanceable Reading') but tiring down a column of statuses and sentences. The rule: sentence case in the UI face; caps only for one- or two-word labels at 11 px or more. (Branch product-ui.md: short column heads and one-word nav group labels may be uppercase at 11–12 px with 0.04–0.06 em tracking; multi-word strings, statuses read in sequence and anything scanned down a column stay sentence case.)
units.quote: The site's small-caps label device as the product's label system
units.whereInMine: anti-patterns.md L104 Typography: "Tracked capitals in a condensed or geometric grotesk at 10–13 px as the label system ... One small-caps device per page at most; the rest sentence case in the text face." Purpose-gated table L62: "Tracked small capitals as a label system | one device per page". design-theory.md C1 L149: "all-caps only for less than a line". audit.mjs flags text under 12 px and uppercase runs over 24 characters. Not covered: the product placements (table heads, status words, stat labels, window bars), the NN/g one-word rationale, and the 'one or two words at ≥ 11 px' rule.
units.conflict: Minor. The branch allows 11 px caps for one or two words, but 2.0's audit.mjs warns on all text under 12 px. Both need to agree (an exemption for single-word uppercase labels, or a 12 px floor everywhere).
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05) or App-UI tells. app-ui.md §3 Density and layout or §5 Tables and lists: the caps rule with the NN/g source.
units.notes: Source: NN/g 'Typography for Glanceable Reading' (listed in the branch product-ui.md sources).

units.title: Serif record names and serif numerals in lists and KPIs; the display face gets one job
units.summary: Failure: a display cut at 18–38 px used for record names in lists and for KPI numerals, where a 15–16 px semibold UI face scans faster. The rule: the display face gets one job, typically the page title (branch product-ui.md adds the sign-in or greeting moment). Panel titles, record names, numbers and labels use the UI face, with weight doing the work (500–600 at 14–16 px).
units.quote: Serif record names and serif numerals in lists and KPIs
units.whereInMine: design-theory.md C2 L160: "Carbon's rule: expressive styles never inside a container". C3 L166: "Assign each face a fixed role". C3 L170: Fraunces and Instrument Serif have no tabular figures. app-ui.md §9: "tabular numerals". Nothing names serif record names or KPI numerals in the display face as a product failure, and nothing says 'the display face gets one job'.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05). app-ui.md §3, or a type paragraph: 'the display face gets one job (page title / sign-in); record names, KPIs and numbers in the UI face at 500–600'.
units.notes: Pairs with the tabular-figures rule. Serif display faces often lack tnum, so serif KPI numerals also fail alignment.

units.title: The marketing hero photograph and tagline on the sign-in screen
units.summary: Failure: the app's sign-in screen reuses the marketing hero photograph and its persuasive tagline. The user is already a customer, and the door is a utility. The rule: form first; brand presence from the mark and at most one abstract graphic derived from it. (Branch product-ui.md cites Linear, Vercel, Stripe's ribbon and Attio, and says a daily user sees that photograph every morning.)
units.quote: The marketing hero photograph and its tagline on the sign-in screen.
units.whereInMine: art-direction.md §6: "Where brand shows — type, colour roles, empty states, onboarding, success moments, marketing-to-product seams". accessibility.md L50 covers sign-in mechanics only (passkeys, paste), and templates/DESIGN.md L145 has 'sign-in approach (passkey / email link; paste allowed)'. imagery.md has no product/app rule. No 2.0 rule covers sign-in imagery or copy.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05). app-ui.md: a new 'Brand moments and doors' paragraph (sign-in, empty states and onboarding as doors, a budget of 2–3 brand moments), from the branch product-ui.md merge. templates/DESIGN.md 'Productive surfaces' → 'where brand is allowed to show' + sign-in treatment.
units.notes: The branch product-ui.md 'doors' and 'brand-moment budget' material is handled by that file's group. Keep this anti-pattern bullet here and link to it.

units.title: 'Windows' and editorial frames copied as decoration around every object
units.summary: Failure: the marketing site's decorative window chrome and editorial frames are put around every object in the app. For example, mono title bars that only repeat the title shown below them.
units.quote: "Windows" and editorial frames copied as decoration
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §1.1: "remove decorative colour from chrome". app-ui.md §1.4: "never a surface nested in a surface". categories.md L27 (marketing): "Do not import from apps: ... UI chrome used as decoration" (the reverse direction). Nothing covers the marketing-to-app direction or redundant title bars.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05), or App-UI tells. It could also go next to 'Card soup' (L115), since both are container decoration.
units.notes: This overlaps P2-01/P2-07 (mono bars). Keep the frame point (redundant chrome) separate from the type point.

units.title: Marketing hairlines on controls fail WCAG 1.4.11
units.summary: A 12–24% (alpha) border reads as refined on a landing page but fails WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1) on an input. Branch product-ui.md: 'a 24 % grey hairline is not enough'; inputs need a visible boundary of at least 3:1 against the surface.
units.quote: Marketing hairlines on controls.
units.whereInMine: The rule is fully in 2.0. accessibility.md §2 L38 Non-text pairs: "3:1 against adjacent colours for input borders ... A light-grey input border (`#e3e3e3` on white = 1.2:1) fails, and no rule engine reports it". a11y.mjs 'nontext' check: "Field boundary contrast too low ... need 3:1". design-theory.md A3: "a hairline only where space cannot". What 2.0 lacks is the anti-pattern framing: the marketing hairline carried onto controls.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05) or App-UI tells: one line pointing to accessibility.md §2 and a11y.mjs nontext.
units.notes: Only the tell needs adding; the rule and its check already exist in 2.0.

units.title: The brand accent used as a focus ring can fail 3:1 on a light ground
units.summary: Using the brand accent as the focus-ring colour on a light ground can fail WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.13 (3:1). Branch product-ui.md: 'the brand accent often fails this on a light ground — use its darker text variant for the ring'.
units.quote: the accent used as a focus ring on a light ground can fail it too
units.whereInMine: accessibility.md §2 L39 Focus token: "One ring: `outline` 2–3 px solid, 2 px offset, ≥ 3:1 against the control and every surface it lands on; a second colour for dark chapters". L37: "A darker accent-for-text token." app-ui.md §2 Focus-visible "3:1 against the unfocused state". a11y.mjs keyboard: '2.4.13 area/contrast estimate'. 2.0 never warns that the accent by default is the likely failure or that the darker text variant is the fix.
units.destination: references/accessibility.md §2 Focus token row: add 'the brand accent often fails on a light ground — use its darker accent-for-text variant'. Plus a line in the anti-patterns transplanted-expression section.

units.title: Contrast checked on the main surface only (hover row, zebra stripe, segmented track, secondary panel)
units.summary: Failure: muted text passes 4.5:1 on the page ground but fails on the hover row, the zebra stripe, the segmented control's track or the secondary panel. Branch product-ui.md adds selected states and dark mode: 'Minimum 4.5:1 on every surface the text sits on'. The branch's technical-qa.md adds a token-matrix contrast check.
units.quote: Contrast checked on the main surface only.
units.whereInMine: accessibility.md §2 L37 Contrast table: "Every text/ground pair actually used, per theme and per chapter, measured on the real ground (`contrast.mjs`)". contrast.mjs computes every fg × bg pair (a token matrix). app-ui.md §2 state matrix Hover: "keep text contrast"; Read-only 4.5:1. 'Per chapter' is marketing vocabulary: 2.0 does not name the product grounds (hover rows, zebra, segmented-control tracks, secondary panels, selected fills) where muted text usually fails.
units.destination: references/accessibility.md §2 Contrast table row: add 'including hover rows, zebra stripes, selected fills, segmented-control tracks and secondary panels on productive surfaces'. A line in the anti-patterns transplanted-expression section or App-UI tells. Optionally, a states.mjs or contrast.mjs recipe for hover/selected grounds.
units.notes: The 1280×800 fold, axe-per-route and token-matrix checks in the branch's technical-qa.md belong to that file's group.

units.title: Marketing whitespace in a product (chapter padding of 100+ px)
units.summary: Failure: marketing chapter padding (100+ px) and generous leads between sections, so the main object (table, board, form) starts below the fold on a laptop.
units.quote: Marketing whitespace.
units.whereInMine: anti-patterns.md L118 App-UI tells: "Low density: 16 px body, 40–48 px controls and 24 px card padding in a *desk* tool used all day" (with the field-tool exception). app-ui.md §3: 'spacing on a 4 px step'. app-ui.md §1.1: "The user's object is the hero". categories.md L35 'Do not import from marketing'. design-theory.md A4 'Whitespace is active' is marketing-oriented ('more than feels comfortable'). None names section or chapter padding or the main object below the fold.
units.conflict: Keep 2.0's field/frontline exception: generous targets and type in a gloved field tool are right there, but 100+ px chapter padding is not right anywhere in a product.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md App-UI tells, the 'Low density' bullet: add 'marketing chapter padding (100+ px) and leads between sections, so the main object starts below the fold'. Or put it in the new transplanted-expression section.
units.notes: design-theory.md A4 'more than feels comfortable' could use a note that this applies to expressive surfaces only.

units.title: Test: on the busiest product screen at 1280 × 800, the first row of the main table, board or form is visible
units.summary: The anti-pattern's test: open the busiest screen at 1280 × 800. If the first row of its main table, board or form is not visible, or anything read daily is under 12 px or in tracked capitals, the marketing site's expression has leaked in.
units.quote: open the product's busiest screen at 1280 × 800. If the first row of its main table, board or form is not visible
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §1 principle 1 (the user's object is the hero). audit.mjs already flags text under 12 px and uppercase strings over 24 characters (inventory.mjs smallText/caps). There is no 1280 × 800 fold check.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md 'App-UI tells' (as the test line)
units.notes: CORRECTION: coverage was 'none'. The half of the test about under-12 px text and caps is already measured by audit.mjs.

units.title: Test: nothing a user reads daily is under 12 px or in tracked capitals
units.summary: The second half of the closing test: if anything a user reads daily is under 12 px, or is set in tracked capitals, the marketing expression has leaked in. Branch product-ui.md: 'Nothing a user must read below 12 px'; 12 px is the floor, and 11 px is allowed only for a single uppercase word.
units.quote: if anything a user reads daily is under 12 px or in tracked capitals, the marketing site's expression has leaked in
units.whereInMine: audit.mjs L264 warns 'Text under 12px' and L265 'Long uppercase runs (> 24 characters)'. The audit.mjs L289 eyebrow count applies to sections. anti-patterns.md L104 has the tracked-capitals label system rule. None of this is framed as a pass/fail test for productive surfaces.
units.conflict: The branch test says 'tracked capitals' for anything read daily, while P2-07 allows caps for one- or two-word labels at ≥ 11 px. The wording should say 'except one- or two-word column or group labels'. 2.0's audit.mjs uses 12 px as the warn threshold without the single-word exemption.
units.destination: references/anti-patterns.md, the test line of the new transplanted-expression section (P2-05). app-ui.md §3 Density and layout: add a '12 px floor for anything read' line. audit.mjs --kind app could raise the under-12 px warning to a signal for app views.

units.title: Branch a11y.mjs as a whole: axe matrix scanner (name collision with 2.0 a11y.mjs)
units.summary: The branch adds a new scripts/a11y.mjs (196 lines, puppeteer-core) that runs axe-core per route x theme x width, with --cookies, --theme-key, --open key chords, a monospace-font check and --allow-mono, scroll-and-finish-animations before each scan, a rule-grouped report, and exit 1 on serious/critical or monospace. 2.0 already has a different scripts/a11y.mjs (683 lines, Playwright). It checks what rule engines miss (keyboard walk, names, reflow, forced colours and more) and says 'Run it AFTER axe'. In 2.0, axe runs inside audit.mjs. Copying the branch file over it would delete all of 2.0's a11y checks.
units.quote: axe-core accessibility scan of a running site or app, per route, per theme,
units.whereInMine: scripts/a11y.mjs (2.0): 'a11y-audit.mjs — scripted checks for the things rule engines (axe, htmlcs, IBM) do not see. Run it AFTER axe'; axe runs in scripts/audit.mjs lines 202-210 ('await page.addScriptTag({ path: axePath })')
units.conflict: Same filename, different job. The branch script is puppeteer-based and takes its own options. 2.0 scripts are Playwright-only and go through lib/env.mjs ('puppeteer is not used'). The branch's docs (technical-qa.md, product-ui.md checklist, SKILL.md commitment 4) all point at 'scripts/a11y.mjs' for the axe matrix, but in 2.0 that job belongs to audit.mjs.
units.destination: Do not add the file. Port its features one by one into scripts/audit.mjs (and states.mjs for the open-state scan), as P3-02..P3-16 describe. Re-point branch docs that name a11y.mjs for axe/themes/mono to audit.mjs.
units.notes: Every feature is listed separately below. Keep 2.0 a11y.mjs unchanged. It could optionally take --dark for its own checks later.

units.title: axe per route x width with WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A+AA + best-practice tags
units.summary: Loops over --paths (default '/') and --widths (default 1440,390) against --base (default http://localhost:3000). It injects axe-core and runs it with runOnly tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa and best-practice.
units.quote: runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa', 'best-practice'] }
units.whereInMine: scripts/audit.mjs --base/--paths/--widths (defaults localhost:3000, ['/'], 1440,390), lines 202-210: same tag set plus experimental 'td-has-header' and 'label-content-name-mismatch' reported as warnings
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs (already there)
units.notes: 2.0 is a superset: same tags plus two experimental rules and resultTypes ['violations'].

units.title: Theme dimension: scan light and dark via prefers-color-scheme (--themes)
units.summary: --themes (default 'light,dark') runs every route and width again with emulated prefers-color-scheme set to each theme name, so dark-mode contrast and other violations get an automated scan.
units.quote: Themes are emulated with prefers-color-scheme;
units.whereInMine: No 2.0 script runs axe or the contrast inventory in dark. capture.mjs --dark only renders ('capture with prefers-color-scheme: dark'). states.mjs can set a state's context {colorScheme:'dark'} but only captures. a11y.mjs uses colorScheme:'dark' only inside its forced-colors pass. Docs require dark contrast by hand: accessibility.md §11 step 10 'Contrast on real renders: dark mode'.
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs: add --themes light,dark (or --dark) that sets browser.newContext({ colorScheme }) per theme and adds -dark to the output slug and the summary heading. Document it in SKILL.md Scripts table (audit.mjs row) and technical-qa.md Accessibility.
units.notes: In Playwright, colorScheme is a context option, so no emulateMediaFeatures call is needed. The contrast inventory in lib/inventory.mjs then covers dark mode for free.

units.title: Scan matrix economy: dark only at widest width, phone widths only in first theme
units.summary: Themes other than the first are scanned only at the widest width, and phone widths run only in the first theme. Two themes x two widths therefore cost 3 scans, not 4.
units.quote: if (theme !== themes[0] && width !== Math.max(...widths)) continue;
units.whereInMine: No theme loop exists in 2.0 audit.mjs (see P3-03).
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs, in the --themes loop from P3-03
units.notes: The header states it: 'Dark mode is scanned at the widest width only; the phone widths run in the first theme.' Port it together with P3-03. A flag could offer the full matrix.

units.title: --theme-key: set the app's stored theme choice in localStorage before each load
units.summary: If the app stores an explicit theme choice, --theme-key <localStorage key> writes the current theme name ('light'/'dark') to that key before each document loads (evaluateOnNewDocument). The app then renders the theme even when it ignores prefers-color-scheme.
units.quote: if the app stores an explicit choice, pass --theme-key <localStorage key>
units.whereInMine: lib/env.mjs --storage ('{"localStorage": {...}}' seeded once per tab before page scripts) can force one fixed theme per run, e.g. two runs with --storage '{"theme":"dark"}'. states.mjs has per-state "storage". Nothing varies the value per theme inside one run.
units.conflict: 2.0 standardises saved state on --storage seeds. A separate --theme-key should build on that rather than add a parallel mechanism.
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs with the --themes loop: --theme-key K adds ctx.addInitScript(localStorage.setItem(K, theme)) per theme context, layered over the --storage seed. Or document in SKILL.md Scripts that a stored theme needs one run per theme with --storage.
units.notes: 2.0 seedStorage writes only once per tab (sessionStorage flag __storage_seeded). A per-theme init script must run after it or use its own context.

units.title: --cookies JSON for signed-in routes
units.summary: --cookies <file> reads a JSON array of cookies and sets them on each page before navigation, so signed-in app routes can be scanned.
units.quote: if (cookies.length) await page.setCookie(...cookies);
units.whereInMine: lib/env.mjs launch(): --storage '{"localStorage":{…},"sessionStorage":{…},"cookies":[{name,value,url}]}' is applied to every context of every script ('await c.addCookies(seed.cookies)'). SKILL.md Scripts: 'every script takes --storage seed.json'.
units.conflict: Branch expects puppeteer cookie objects. Playwright addCookies needs url, or domain+path.
units.destination: lib/env.mjs --storage (already there)
units.notes: Optionally note in SKILL.md that a cookie exported from DevTools needs 'url' or 'domain'+'path'.

units.title: Signed-in scans: mint a session server-side, never type credentials into the page
units.summary: To reach signed-in routes, create the session server-side (a session cookie or token) and pass it in. The agent never types credentials into the page's login form.
units.quote: never type credentials into the page
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md Scripts: 'Pages that depend on saved state — ... a signed-in view ... every script takes --storage seed.json'. SKILL.md 'Only when blocked...: credentials' treats credentials as something the user provides. No rule on how to get a session or on typing credentials.
units.destination: SKILL.md 'Scripts' paragraph on --storage (and technical-qa.md Functional checks): 'for a signed-in view, mint a session server-side (seed script, test user, CLI) and put the cookie in the seed; never type credentials into the page'.
units.notes: One short sentence. Useful for app surfaces, where most routes sit behind auth.

units.title: --open: scan overlays in their open state (key chord per path)
units.summary: --open "/path=Control+k" presses the chord on that path after the first scan (modifiers held down, last key pressed, released in reverse). It waits 400 ms and scans again, labelled '+open'. Command palettes, menus and dialogs exist only while open, so a closed-state scan misses them. Desktop widths only (skipped when width < 768).
units.quote: and scans again, because palettes, menus and dialogs only exist when open.
units.whereInMine: states.mjs can reach the open state with steps ({"press": "Control+k"}, click) and capture it, and --aria writes the accessibility tree. widgets.mjs checks dialog/menu keyboard contracts. accessibility.md 'Tool gotchas': 'axe skips closed dialogs, so contracts must open things to test them'. Nothing runs axe or the contrast inventory in an open state.
units.destination: scripts/states.mjs: add --axe (inject axe via resolveModule('axe-core/axe.min.js') after the steps and report violations per state). This generalises --open to any click/press/fill path. Alternatively add --open 'path=Chord' to audit.mjs. Mention in technical-qa.md Accessibility and accessibility.md §10.
units.notes: Playwright's keyboard.press('Control+K') handles chords natively, so the manual down/press/up code is not needed. Keep the rule 'scan palettes, menus and dialogs open'.

units.title: Monospace check: fail on any rendered monospace text unless --allow-mono
units.summary: For every element with its own text node, reads the first family of the computed font-family. It flags the element if that family matches /mono|courier|consolas|menlo|monaco|code/i or equals 'monospace'. It prints up to 6 offenders per view (tag.class "text" (family)), counts the views, and exits 1 unless --allow-mono is passed for a product whose users read code. Rationale: a code font reads as 'code' to anyone who is not a developer.
units.quote: const MONO = /mono|courier|consolas|menlo|monaco|code/i;
units.whereInMine: The rule exists without a check: anti-patterns.md purpose-gated table 'Monospace | developer or infrastructure products, code, true machine identifiers | the sans with tabular-nums'; art-direction.md 'Monospace only for developer and infrastructure products'; categories.md dev tools 'Monospace belongs here'. The scripts only flag saturated mono faces (geist mono, jetbrains mono...) as a signal at >= 10% share (audit.mjs 'Saturated face(s)'). Nothing fails on monospace.
units.conflict: 2.0 lets monospace carry 'true machine identifiers' with a written reason. The branch (commitment 4) forbids it for IDs, passwords, env names, placeholders, key hints and timers unless the audience reads code. Also 2.0 has --kind docs where mono is legitimate, so the allowance should key off --kind docs plus an explicit --allow-mono.
units.destination: lib/inventory.mjs (collect mono text elements next to 'families') + scripts/audit.mjs (F entry 'Monospace text rendered: …' unless --allow-mono or --kind docs). Document in SKILL.md Scripts table and anti-patterns.md Monospace row.
units.notes: The rule itself (commitment 4, the lessons rows) belongs to other groups (SKILL.md, lessons.md). This unit is the check. The 'code' regex also matches Fira Code and Source Code Pro, as intended.

units.title: Browser default monospace for code/kbd/samp/pre counts too
units.summary: Browsers set code, kbd, samp and pre in monospace by default. The check reads computed fonts, so it catches faces nobody chose (e.g. Ctrl K / Esc key hints in <kbd>) as well as chosen ones. The fix is to point the framework's mono token and those elements at the UI face.
units.quote: so this catches faces nobody chose as well as ones somebody did.
units.whereInMine: No 2.0 file mentions browser-default monospace for code/kbd/samp/pre (rg 'kbd' finds nothing in references).
units.destination: anti-patterns.md 'Purpose-gated techniques' Monospace row, or design-theory.md C3 Voice: 'the browser's default monospace on code/kbd/samp/pre counts; set them to the UI face'. The audit.mjs check from P3-09 reads computed fonts.
units.notes: Came from the Brio3 app lesson (Ctrl K / Esc hints rendered in the default mono). The lesson row itself is in lessons.md, another group.

units.title: 'faces rendered' summary across all views
units.summary: Collects the first computed family of every text-bearing element across all scanned views and prints 'faces rendered: …' at the end.
units.quote: console.log(`\nfaces rendered: ${[...faces].join(', ')}`);
units.whereInMine: audit.mjs summary per page/width: 'Families (declared): ${family} ${share}%' from lib/inventory.mjs (first family of computed font-family of each visible text element, weighted by characters), plus 'Declared font families not available — the page renders in a fallback'
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs (already there)
units.notes: 2.0 is richer: share by characters, and it flags families that did not load.

units.title: Scroll through the page before scanning so scroll-triggered reveals fire
units.summary: Before each scan, scrolls from top to bottom in steps of max(200, 0.8 x innerHeight) with 60 ms pauses, then returns to the top. A scan taken before reveals fire reads not-yet-revealed or mid-fade text as low contrast. This was seen on a live site at 390 px, where the section sat below the fold.
units.quote: (seen on a live site at 390, where the section sat below the fold).
units.whereInMine: lib/env.mjs settle()/settleOnce(): 'scroll in viewport steps so observers fire and lazy images load' (step max(200, 0.8 x innerHeight), 120 ms, lazy to eager, then top), called by audit.mjs before focus walk and axe. growToDocument, then waitForTimeout(250) + finishMotion. lessons.md 2026-09-28 'axe contrast failures on text they had themselves set fading'.
units.destination: lib/env.mjs settle (already there)
units.notes: If states.mjs gains --axe (P3-08), call settle() before scanning there too. 2.0's a11y.mjs newPage() does not scroll, but it does not run axe.

units.title: Zero all CSS animation/transition durations and delays before scanning
units.summary: After scrolling, injects a style that sets animation-duration, animation-delay, transition-duration and transition-delay to 0s !important on every element and pseudo-element, then waits 300 ms. Entrance animations end at their final state, and anything triggered later (e.g. an overlay opened by --open) appears instantly. Infinite CSS animations collapse to their base style instead of freezing mid-cycle.
units.quote: animation-duration:0s!important;animation-delay:0s!important;transition-duration:0s!important
units.whereInMine: lib/env.mjs finishMotion(): finishes every finite animation from document.getAnimations() (CSS animations and transitions included) and pauses infinite ones. audit.mjs calls it after settle and again after growToDocument. states.mjs calls it after each step. No CSS override.
units.destination: lib/env.mjs: an optional freezeMotion(page) that adds the zero-duration style tag. Call it in audit.mjs before axe/inventory and in states.mjs --axe before scanning.
units.notes: Two gaps in 2.0. Infinite animations paused mid-frame (e.g. a pulsing opacity) can leave text at a low alpha when contrast is read. Transitions that start after finishMotion ran (late observers) are not covered. Low priority, since finishMotion already handles the common case.

units.title: Finish script-driven (element.animate) animations; leave infinite ones
units.summary: The CSS override misses animations started from script, so it calls document.getAnimations().forEach(a => a.finish()). Infinite ones throw and are left alone. Waits 200 ms before scanning.
units.quote: CSS overrides miss animations started from script (element.animate):
units.whereInMine: lib/env.mjs finishMotion(): 'if (a.effect?.getComputedTiming?.().iterations === Infinity) a.pause(); else a.finish();'
units.destination: lib/env.mjs finishMotion (already there)
units.notes: Infinite animations differ: 2.0 pauses them, the branch leaves them running. See P3-13.

units.title: Exit non-zero on serious/critical axe violations (and on monospace)

F : W).push(`axe-core: …`)'). 2.0 a11y.mjs exits 1 on FAIL; widgets.mjs and states.mjs also set exitCode. Gate in technical-qa.md and accessibility.md §12: 'axe 0 violations'.

units.title: Lesson row 2026-09-25 Brio3 app: marketing expression carried into the product
units.summary: New table row. Project: 'Brio3 app (Next.js product, matched to brio3.com)'. What went wrong: the first pass put the marketing site's expression into the application: 40 px serif titles with eyebrows and two-line leads on every page, 10.5 px tracked mono capitals as the label system for bars, table heads and statuses, serif record names and KPI numerals, and the site's hero photograph and tagline on the sign-in screen. The user said the app is used all day, again and again, so usability, accessibility, readability, efficiency and visual comfort come first; the site's typography, sizes, spacing and layout should not be copied; the app needs an image that suits it. Root cause: the skill declared itself 'not for application UI' and had no product mode, so the family test was applied as 'replicate the site'. Nothing separated identity (transferable) from expression (marketing-only), and contrast checks stopped at the main ground, missing WCAG 1.4.11 for inputs and focus rings. What changed: Phase 0 'Classify the surface' in SKILL.md; new references/product-ui.md (productive vs expressive type with Carbon and Material 3 numbers, density, navigation and accelerators, component and data states, WCAG 2.2 for heavy use, visual comfort, brand moments and sign-in); 'Marketing expression transplanted into a product' in anti-patterns.md; 'When the surface is an application' in art-direction.md; the task audit in audit.md §3c; 'Surface' and 'Product UI' in templates/DESIGN.md; application checks (axe per route, keyboard walk, token-matrix contrast, 1280 × 800 fold) in technical-qa.md.

units.title: Identity transfers from the marketing site to the product; expression does not
units.summary: The fix behind P4-01's root cause. A marketing site supplies the product's identity (mark, colours and their meanings, the display face for one job, the status vocabulary) and never its expression (display sizes, spacing, layouts, eyebrow-plus-lead stacks, editorial chapters, hero imagery, taglines, decorative motion). The family test runs against the site's identity, not its layout, so 'match the site' never means 'replicate the site'.

Missing: the explicit identity vs expression lists, and a guard on audit.md §4 'The brand family' and the logo-design family test so a sibling site is not copied into a product.

units.title: Visual comfort for long sessions
units.summary: The row cites product-ui.md §6 and the user's words 'visual comfort'. Offer light and dark themes, following the OS and remembering the choice (NN/g: light mode reads better for most people; dark mode helps people with cataracts and in dim rooms). Never pure black, and lift dark-mode text (halation). A warm or off-white ground reads calmer than #fff over hours. Keep saturated fields out of the work area. Consistency is comfort. Nothing animates for attention except live state. Transitions ≤ 200 ms.

units.title: Mono exceptions removed from art direction ('a data/mono face if the concept wants one')
units.summary: The branch changed art-direction.md in two places. The typography decision became 'a monospace face only for a developer or infrastructure product whose users read code — never as a label, data or values face otherwise, and never carried over from a sibling site'. The 'Technical / instrument' family became '... monospace details only when the audience itself reads code (commitment 4)'.
units.quote: `art-direction.md` invited "a data/mono face if the concept wants one"

The 2.0 text no longer has 'a data/mono face if the concept wants one', but design-theory.md C3 says 'a third (data or code) only for a technical product' and templates/DESIGN.md says 'Data / code face, if any, and why.'

units.destination: skills/website-redesign/references/art-direction.md §3 (Technical / instrument) and §4 Typography: the gate becomes 'the audience reads code'. design-theory.md C3: 'a third (code) only when the audience reads code; never a data face'.

units.title: Tabular figures are not a monospace font

units.title: Script check: fail on rendered monospace text unless --allow-mono
units.summary: The branch's a11y.mjs reads the computed font-family of every text element in each view. It flags elements whose first family matches /mono|courier|consolas|menlo|monaco|code/i or is the generic 'monospace', and lists up to 6 examples (tag.class "text" (family)). It counts views with monospace and exits 1 unless `--allow-mono` is passed. The header comment explains that browsers set code / kbd / samp / pre in monospace by default.
units.quote: `scripts/a11y.mjs` now reads the computed font of every text element and fails on monospace unless `--allow-mono`
units.whereInMine: The 2.0 scripts/a11y.mjs is a different script (CDP names, outline, keyboard, pointer, targets, nontext, autocomplete, reflow, spacing, forced, colour, motion) with no font check. 2.0 audit.mjs lists 'web fonts loaded' and saturated faces, and scripts/lib/inventory.mjs reads `cs.fontFamily` (line ~100), but nothing flags monospace.
units.conflict: Architecture: the branch's a11y.mjs is a standalone axe runner, while 2.0 scripts use lib/env.mjs (launch/open), --storage seeding and FAIL/WARN/INFO output. Port the check, not the file.
units.destination: skills/website-redesign/scripts/lib/inventory.mjs (collect monospace text) and audit.mjs (FAIL unless `--allow-mono`), or a 'fonts' section in the 2.0 a11y.mjs. Document it in the SKILL.md scripts table and technical-qa.md gates.
units.notes: Improve on the branch regex: also match `ui-monospace`, and detect a fallback to monospace when a named family is missing (inventory.mjs already has width-comparison code against 'monospace'). This is 2.0's own 'if the lesson is mechanical, put it in a script' rule applied. The scripts group owns it; it is listed so P4-02's last column stays true.

units.title: A rule the user has had to repeat becomes a commitment without exceptions (implicit in P4-02)

The branch's response was to turn the third repeat into a no-exception commitment plus a script check. It did not edit 'Learning from corrections' to state this as a general method.

units.whereInMine: SKILL.md 'Learning from corrections' #2: 'If the lesson is mechanical, put it in a script — prose that describes a check the tools do not perform is how the capture bug survived three lessons.' This covers the script half, not the escalation to a commitment.

units.notes: Derived. The branch did not edit this section, so treat it as optional; the lesson row (P4-02) carries the evidence either way.

Every entry came from a user correction…'), the table header and all 20 origin/main rows unchanged. The only content change is the two added 2026-09-25 rows. The branch adds no digest.
