units.title: New reference: discovery.md (Phase 0 for thin context)
units.summary: A new 120-line reference, 'Phase 0 — Discovery (when context is thin)', with sections §1 Triage, §2 Social media as brand input, §3 Learning an unfamiliar domain, §4 References when none were supplied, §5 When the website is becoming an application, §5b Signature experiences, §5c When an experimental prototype overtakes the original, §6 Greenfield architecture, §7 Project memory, §8 Permissions. Its outputs are research documents plus a product definition (templates/PRODUCT.md). Phases 1–8 then run as usual. It came from commits b719146, af235e9 and 1de7810 (The Cake Junction: an Instagram-only bakery that became a site, a builder and a back office).
units.quote: # Phase 0 — Discovery (when context is thin)
units.whereInMine: No equivalent file. Closest is references/framing.md ('# Phase 0 — Frame the problem'), which classifies routes, intensity and top tasks but assumes an existing site/repo.
units.conflict: Name clash: 2.0 already calls Phase 0 'Frame'. The branch title 'Phase 0 — Discovery' would give the skill two Phase 0s. Its internal references ('Phase 1's company audit', 'Phases 1–8') use 1.x wording. It uses `research/…` for project research, but 2.0 SKILL.md reserves `research/…` for the skill repo's evidence folder. tools/check-skill.mjs requires every '`discovery.md` §N' to match a '## N.' heading, so keep '## 5b.' and '## 5c.' as they are.
units.destination: skills/website-redesign/references/discovery.md (new), retitled as a Phase 0 companion to framing.md, e.g. 'Phase 0 (continued) — Discovery, when context is thin'. Link it from framing.md, the SKILL.md Phase 0 row/paragraph, and the knowledge-base table row for framing/categories.
units.notes: Port the whole file, then apply the per-section reconciliations in the units below. A matching lesson row (2026-09-26 The Cake Junction, 'no discovery phase for thin context') sits in the branch's lessons.md, which another group inventories.

units.title: Thin context: build the missing context before designing
units.summary: Governing principle: the less reliable product and design context the brief gives you, the more deliberately you must build that context before designing. Otherwise a designer who starts drawing produces the category's template. It appears as the discovery.md epigraph and is repeated in the SKILL.md triage paragraph.
units.quote: The less reliable product and design context you are given, the more deliberately you build that context yourself before designing.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §6: 'The brief is short — half a page. If it cannot be written, the redesign is not ready to start, and the gap is the first thing to tell the user.' That tells the user about the gap but never says to go and build the context.
units.destination: discovery.md epigraph, plus one sentence in the SKILL.md '### Phase 0 — Frame' paragraph (and optionally framing.md §6, after 'If it cannot be written…': 'when context is thin, build it: discovery.md').
units.notes: Keep it short in SKILL.md, because the description is already near its limit and the Phase 0 paragraph is dense.

units.title: Discovery replaces the missing audit; what the customer meets today stands in for 'the old site'
units.summary: When there is no site, Phases 1–8 run as usual, with 'the old site' replaced by what the customer meets today: the social profile, a competitor's template, a PDF menu. SKILL.md says the profile or the competitor's template 'plays the part of "the old site" in every later check'.
units.quote: with "the old site" replaced by whatever the customer meets today (the social profile, a competitor's template, a PDF menu)
units.whereInMine: No home. Several 2.0 checks need a rendered old build: parity.mjs (--before URL required; the Phase 8 gate 'no unsourced claim and no lost route, id or form field'), perf.mjs --before, states.json written 'against the old build', the distance test (the five first-notice things of the current site), before/after captures, and task walkthroughs 'on the old build and the new one'.
units.conflict: None of the 2.0 old-vs-new scripts can take a social profile or a PDF as the 'before', and the Phase 8 gate is written as parity against the old build. Without a stated substitute, a greenfield run either fails the gate or skips it silently. Needed: a greenfield clause that sources claims through parity.mjs --source against the brand-audit and caption export and the owner's answers, with no route, id or form parity, and that runs the distance test against the category template or competitor.
units.destination: Discovery reference ('old site' substitute paragraph), technical-qa.md Parity section, and the SKILL.md Phase 8 gate (greenfield clause)
units.notes: CORRECTION: coverage 'none' stands, but the conflict with 2.0's old-build gates was not recorded. The Phase 1 audit.mjs 'before' baseline does not exist in the greenfield case either.

units.title: Triage: decide how much discovery is needed in the first minutes, in writing
units.summary: §1 opens with a triage table (Situation, Signals, What to add before designing). It is decided in the first minutes and written down, and several rows can apply at once. The rows are units G1-05 to G1-11.
units.quote: Decide in the first minutes, in writing. Several rows can apply.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1 (classify every route) and §2 (choose the intensity) are the closest Phase 0 steps. Neither asks how thin the context is.
units.conflict: 2.0's intensity vocabulary (refine / redesign / rethink) assumes something exists. A first site or 'no site; the brand lives on social media' has no intensity value. Either add a fourth value (e.g. 'new' / 'create') to framing.md §2 and the DESIGN.md brief table, or state that greenfield runs as 'rethink' with no baseline.
units.destination: discovery.md §1, with one pointer line in framing.md (e.g. a step 0 before '## 1. Classify every route', or in the intro) and in the SKILL.md Phase 0 paragraph.
units.notes: The triage fits naturally as the first act of 2.0's Frame phase.

units.title: Triage row: redesign of a working site needs no discovery
units.summary: In the triage table, 'Redesign of a working site' (signals: a repo, a clear product, known customers) adds nothing: 'Phase 1 is enough.' The SKILL.md triage paragraph repeats this as 'A redesign of a working site starts at Phase 1.'
units.quote: Nothing. Phase 1 is enough.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md Workflow: every job starts at '0. Frame'. The small-job path is '0 → 1 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 8, never skipping 0 or 6', and framing.md says 'Read before anything else.'
units.conflict: In 2.0, Phase 0 is Frame and is never skipped. Copied verbatim, 'Phase 1 is enough' and 'starts at Phase 1' would tell the agent to skip framing. The meaning (no discovery needed) fits 2.0; the phase number does not.
units.destination: Discovery triage table, reworded to 'Nothing beyond Frame and Audit'; same rewording in the SKILL.md triage paragraph (G1-91)
units.notes: CORRECTION: was 'full'. 2.0 covers the meaning by default, but the branch's wording contradicts 2.0's never-skip-Phase-0 gate.

units.title: Triage row: no site, the brand lives on social media
units.summary: Signal: an Instagram, TikTok or Facebook page is the main asset. Add the §2 social audit. The profile is both the old site and the brand guidelines.
units.quote: | **No site; the brand lives on social media** | An Instagram/TikTok/Facebook page is the main asset | §2 social audit: the profile *is* the old site and the brand guidelines |
units.whereInMine: No social-media guidance anywhere in 2.0 (rg for instagram/social media/tiktok returns nothing relevant).
units.destination: discovery.md §1 triage table.

units.title: Triage row: unfamiliar domain
units.summary: Signal: you cannot list the variables a customer chooses, or what the operator needs in order to act. Add §3 domain research and continue until you can.
units.quote: | **Unfamiliar domain** | You cannot list the variables a customer chooses, or what the operator needs to act | §3 domain research until you can |
units.whereInMine: framing.md §5 question bank (Users, Tasks and hierarchy, Reality) is generic. It has no domain-learning trigger or stop condition.
units.destination: discovery.md §1 triage table.

units.title: Triage row: no references supplied
units.summary: Signal: the brief says only something like 'Make it premium' or 'like a real studio did it'. Add §4 references: direct competitors, an adjacent problem, and one deliberately different tone.
units.quote: | **No references supplied** | "Make it premium", "like a real studio did it" | §4 references: direct, adjacent-problem, and one deliberately different |
units.whereInMine: research.md 'Choose references by problem' already builds a set without user references ('The reference the user named, if any').
units.destination: discovery.md §1 triage table (the row can point straight at research.md).
units.notes: Because 2.0 research.md already chooses by problem, discovery §4 can shrink to a pointer plus the interaction-problem addition (G1-31).

units.title: Triage row and signals: the website is becoming an application
units.summary: Signals: a transaction needs a human decision (quote, approval, booking), customers have their own state, an operator runs a daily workflow, or capacity is finite. Response: design both sides around one shared record (§5) and write templates/PRODUCT.md.
units.quote: Orders need a human decision (quote, approval, booking), per-customer state, an operator workflow, capacity
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1: 'Most repositories hold more than one kind of surface — a marketing site and an app, a storefront and an account area … Classify per route or route group', with the Ecommerce and SaaS app categories. This covers mixtures that already exist, not spotting an application that does not exist yet behind a brochure site.
units.destination: framing.md §1 (the signals next to per-route classification), pointing to discovery §5 and PRODUCT.md
units.notes: CORRECTION: was 'none'. 2.0 already classifies marketing and app surfaces per route; what is new is the forward-looking signals and the operator side.

units.title: Triage row: greenfield stack
units.summary: Signal: an empty folder, or 'choose the foundation'. Add §6: record the architecture decision before scaffolding.
units.quote: | **Greenfield stack** | Empty folder, "choose the foundation" | §6 architecture decision recorded before scaffolding |
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md Phase 5: 'Stay in the existing framework'. design-systems.md §1: 'Detect before choosing. In an existing repo the component layer is already chosen.'
units.conflict: 2.0 assumes an existing stack everywhere. The greenfield exception has to be stated explicitly so the 'stay in the existing framework' rule does not block it.
units.destination: discovery.md §1 triage table.

units.title: Triage row: long-running, multi-session work
units.summary: Signals: a big scope, and the user expects to come back later. Add §7: project memory from day one.
units.quote: | **Long-running, multi-session work** | Big scope, the user expects to return later | §7 project memory from day one |
units.whereInMine: No project-memory guidance in 2.0.
units.destination: discovery.md §1 triage table.

units.title: How much discovery is enough: every topic ends in a written consequence
units.summary: Discovery is not a timer. Stop researching a topic once it has changed a decision and further reading would not change another. Every topic must end in a written consequence ('servings in the customer's words, not diameters', 'quote-first, not checkout'). A topic that changed no decision was browsing: keep the research, drop the topic.
units.quote: Stop researching a topic when it has changed a decision and further reading would not change another.
units.whereInMine: No stop rule in 2.0. research.md says 'Extract principles, then put the references away', which is the nearest discipline.
units.destination: discovery.md §1 ('How much is enough').
units.notes: This could also serve research.md as a general stop rule.

units.title: Social audit 1: study the profile like an archive; collect every post programmatically
units.summary: When the profile is the brand, study it like an archive, not a feed. Scrolling and eyeballing only samples the newest dozen posts. Pull every post's image URL and caption from the page DOM into structured data, and the story highlights frame by frame. Then download the media, with the user's permission, into a local research folder that is neither shipped nor committed. Social pages block most export paths (CSP, popups, downloads). A form POST to a local receiver, or reading the DOM in chunks, usually works.
units.quote: Pull every post's image URL and caption from the page DOM into structured data (and the story highlights frame by frame)
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0. Its scripts (Playwright with lib/env.mjs) capture and audit pages but do not harvest social profiles.
units.conflict: 2.0 SKILL.md says 'If the lesson is mechanical, put it in a script'. Here collection is prose only, with no tool. Any script port must respect the §8 permissions rule and platform terms.
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 1.
units.notes: A possible later script: a Playwright harvester that uses lib/env.mjs and `--storage` for a logged-in session and writes posts.json plus media into a local, git-ignored folder. It does not exist in either branch, so this stays a note, not a port.

units.title: Social audit 2: numbered contact sheets of every image
units.summary: Tile every image with its index and look at all of it. The numbers let you cite evidence ('posts 000–060 share one backdrop') and pick heroes later.
units.quote: **Contact sheets, numbered.** Tile every image with its index and look at all of it.
units.whereInMine: imagery.md 'Sourcing in practice': 'build contact sheets (a grid of thumbnails with their ids). Choose from the sheet'. That is for stock candidates, not for auditing a client's archive. compare.mjs builds grids ('Before/after sheets').
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 2, with a pointer to compare.mjs --grid if it can tile arbitrary images with labels.
units.notes: Check whether compare.mjs --grid accepts a folder of images with index labels. If it does, name it here.

units.title: Social audit 3: census, then signature versus bread-and-butter
units.summary: Count what the business actually makes, by category. Then separate the signature work (recognisably theirs) from the bread-and-butter work (pays the bills, looks like everyone else's). Lead the site with the signature and give the rest a category.
units.quote: Then separate the **signature** (the work that is recognisably theirs) from the **bread-and-butter** (what pays the bills and looks like everyone else's).
units.whereInMine: audit.md §2: 'the differentiator versus the obvious alternatives' and 'What should a visitor remember?'. These are conceptual. There is no census of the actual output.
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 3.

units.title: Social audit 4: photography eras and sets; sample colours from the photos
units.summary: Most accounts have eras (kitchen bench, then a white cloth, then a proper backdrop). The newest consistent set is often a stronger identity asset than the logo. Sample its colours from the photos the way you sample a logo, and consider staging the site the way they stage their photos.
units.quote: The newest consistent set is often a stronger identity asset than the logo. **Sample its colours from the photos** like you sample a logo
units.whereInMine: audit.md §1: '**Sample the logo's actual colours** (`scripts/palette.mjs --from logo.svg`)'. palette.mjs also takes a PNG raster ('--from logo.png # dominant colours in a raster'). art-direction.md §1 'Sources of form' has no photo-set source. imagery.md: 'wait for the owners' photographs'.
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 4, plus a clause in audit.md §1 'Brand assets' and art-direction.md §1 'Sources of form' (the client's own photo set as a source of palette and staging).
units.notes: Script note: palette.mjs raster sampling uses pngjs only (PNG). Social media photos are JPEG, so either convert them first or add JPEG support. The branch's lessons row (2026-09-26 'sample the backdrop') and imagery.md 'The client's own photographs' belong to other groups.

units.title: Social audit 5: when the logo and the work disagree, follow the work
units.summary: Social-first businesses often have a logo made before their style matured (clip-art, generated, multicolour). When the logo and the work disagree, follow the work. Keep the logo's meaningful parts (name, lockup, a colour, a motif), and put any refinement to the owner as a proposal.
units.quote: When the logo and the work disagree, follow the work, keep the logo's meaningful parts (name, lockup, a colour, a motif), and put any refinement to the owner as a proposal.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md commitment 3: 'Sample the logo and wordmark and look at the brand family before choosing any colour or typeface.' art-direction.md §4 Colour: 'Keep the brand's hue family unless the user says the identity is the problem.' art-direction.md §5 category test: 'the assets win'. logo-design.md: 'Nothing is applied until the user picks.'
units.conflict: 2.0 treats the logo as the first and winning brand asset unless the user says the identity is the problem. The branch lets the body of work outrank a weak logo without the user saying so, while keeping the logo's meaningful parts and routing changes to the owner. They agree that any logo change is only a proposal.
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 5, plus a sentence in SKILL.md commitment 3 or art-direction.md §4 Colour: 'for social-first brands whose logo predates their style, the newest consistent photo set counts as a brand asset alongside the logo; refinements to the mark are proposals'.

units.title: Social audit 6: highlights and pinned posts are the FAQ, price list, reviews and policies
units.summary: Read every frame: size or serving charts, 'how to order', customer messages (real proof, usable verbatim with permission), and process videos.
units.quote: **Highlights and pinned posts are the FAQ, price list, reviews and policies.**
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md commitment 2 ('only what exists in the repo or from the user') and audit.md §2 ('What real proof exists') define proof, but not where to find it when there is no repo.
units.conflict: parity.mjs only counts a quote or price as sourced if it appears in the old site or `--source` dirs. Transcribe highlights and customer messages into the local research folder and pass it as `--source`, or every real testimonial will be flagged as unsourced.
units.destination: discovery.md §2 item 6, plus a note in technical-qa.md 'Parity with the old site' about sourcing claims from transcribed social content.

units.title: Social audit 7: take the voice from the captions
units.summary: Note person (first or third), tone, humour, spelling habits and the phrases customers repeat back. The site's copy should sound like the owner on a good day, not like an agency.
units.quote: The site's copy should sound like the owner on a good day, not like an agency.

units.title: Social audit 8: learn the customers from captions and tags

units.title: The brand-audit write-up cites post numbers and replaces the Phase 1 company audit

units.conflict: The research/ path means two different things. In 2.0, `research/…` is the skill repository's own evidence folder. The branch uses research/ for the client project's working folder: the brand audit, domain notes and raw downloads kept uncommitted (§2.1, §8), 'the raw research in the project's research folder' (realtime-3d §9), and the PRODUCT.md header 'Written <date> from `research/…`'. After the merge, an agent reading 'research/…' cannot tell which folder is meant. Rename the project folder (for example discovery/) or always say 'the project's research folder'. Separately, 'replaces Phase 1's company audit' still conflicts with 2.0 Phase 1, as the inventory already recorded.

units.title: Domain 1: map the configuration variables and their dependencies
units.summary: Research the domain until you can say, without guessing, what a customer chooses, what each option depends on, and which choices only appear after another. Progressive disclosure comes from the dependency graph, not from taste.
units.quote: (progressive disclosure comes from the dependency graph, not from taste)
units.whereInMine: ui-ux.md §progressive disclosure: 'show what most people need most of the time; put the rest one click away… never more than two levels'. It does not derive disclosure from dependencies.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 1, with a cross-reference from ui-ux.md progressive-disclosure bullet.

units.title: Domain 2: the customer's words versus the trade's words
units.summary: Customers say 'how many people', 'heart-shaped', 'less sweet'; the trade says '8-inch double barrel', 'Lambeth'. Design in the customer's vocabulary and use the trade term only as a hint label.
units.quote: Design in the first vocabulary, and label with the second only as a hint.
units.whereInMine: ui-ux.md §1 Nielsen #2: 'the users' words, not ours; no jargon'. framing.md §4: 'labels come from here, not from the org chart'.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 2.
units.notes: This adds the 'trade term as a secondary hint' nuance, which 2.0 does not have.

units.title: Domain 3: the workflow from first contact to fulfilment
units.summary: Map which steps need a human, what information is required before each one, and where orders stall.
units.quote: From first contact to fulfilment: which steps need a human, what information is required before each one, and where orders stall.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §4: 'For each top task note the start, the end, the steps and decisions'. audit.md §3 walks tasks in the running product. Neither covers the operator/human side of the workflow.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 3.

units.title: Domain 4: pricing mechanics; never invent prices; design for unknown prices
units.summary: Learn what drives price (and what barely does), whether a price can be computed or must be quoted, and the local range. Never invent a business's prices, and design the UI to work honestly when prices are unknown.
units.quote: Never invent a business's prices. Design the UI to work honestly when prices are unknown.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md commitment 2 ('prices… only what exists in the repo or from the user'). implementation.md: 'never change a claim, a number, a name or a price without the user'. SKILL.md 'When to stop and ask': 'a fact the repo cannot answer (a price…)'.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 4.
units.notes: New in substance: understand pricing mechanics, and design a UI that works when prices are unknown.

units.title: Domain 5: capacity and time
units.summary: Learn the lead times, what a day or week can hold, rush rules and seasonality.
units.quote: **Capacity and time.** Lead times, what a day or week can hold, rush rules, seasonality.
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 5.

units.title: Domain 6: physical and regulatory constraints
units.summary: Transport, storage, heat, allergens and licensing become care instructions, validation, and things the site must not claim.
units.quote: These become care instructions, validation and things the site must not claim.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §5 Honesty: 'What would a regulator, a support agent or a lawyer flag?'. categories.md Fintech covers regulatory text for finance only.
units.destination: discovery.md §3 bullet 6.

units.title: The domain document records only what changed a decision, with sources
units.summary: The output of domain research is a short document that records only what changed a decision, with its sources.
units.quote: The output is a short domain document that records **only what changed a decision**, with its sources.
units.whereInMine: No domain document in 2.0. The DESIGN.md Brief has constraints and assumptions.
units.conflict: The research-folder name again (see G1-22).
units.destination: discovery.md §3 closing line.

units.title: References 1: choose for the problem; local direct competitors for market structure and price bands
units.summary: Choose references for the problem, not the category. Direct competitors in the same city or niche teach the market's structure, its price bands and what customers already expect.
units.quote: **Direct competitors** in the same city or niche, to learn the market's structure and price bands, and what customers already expect.
units.whereInMine: research.md 'Choose references by problem' plus 'Two or three direct competitors or the closest adjacent category (see what the category expects — Jakob's law…)'. It does not mention local competitors or price bands.
units.destination: research.md 'Choose references by problem' (add 'in the same city or niche; note price bands'). discovery.md §4 becomes a pointer.

units.title: References 2: adjacent products that solved the same interaction problem
units.summary: Study products that solved the same interaction problem: configurators (rings, sofas, sneakers), template personalisation (invitations, cards), quote-and-approve flows (tradespeople, event vendors), and booking with capacity (salons, tours).
units.quote: **Adjacent products that solved the same interaction problem**: configurators (rings, sofas, sneakers), template personalisation (invitations, cards), quote-and-approve flows (tradespeople, event vendors), booking with capacity (salons, tours).
units.whereInMine: research.md: 'One or two best-in-class examples outside the category whose *problem* is similar.' Its problem examples ('Show a complex product simply'…) are presentation problems, not interaction problems like configure, quote or book.
units.destination: research.md 'Choose references by problem', as a bullet merged with G1-96.
units.notes: This duplicates the research.md hunk (G1-96). Merge once in research.md and point to it from discovery.md §4.

units.title: References 3: one deliberately different tone
units.summary: Include one reference with a deliberately different tone, so the direction is chosen rather than defaulted.
units.quote: **One deliberately different tone**, so the direction is chosen rather than defaulted.
units.whereInMine: research.md: 'One deliberately contrary reference, so the direction is chosen rather than defaulted.'
units.destination: research.md (already present).

units.title: References 4: record shape Reference → Useful because → Lesson we apply → Deliberately not taken
units.summary: When no references were supplied, record each chosen reference as Reference → Useful because → Lesson we apply → Deliberately not taken. A list of URLs is not research.
units.quote: Record each as **Reference → Useful because → Lesson we apply → Deliberately not taken**. A list of URLs is not research.
units.whereInMine: templates/DESIGN.md References table: 'Reference | Problem it solves | Taken (as a principle) | Deliberately not taken'.
units.conflict: Vocabulary only: different column names for the same 2.0 table.
units.destination: Discovery reference §4: point to the DESIGN.md References table and use its column names
units.notes: CORRECTION: 'full' stands; the conflict field should record the naming clash (see G1-97).

units.title: References 5: if the browser pane will not render, read the page text
units.summary: When a browser pane will not render (hidden or throttled), read the page text. Structure and copy are often enough for an interaction reference.
units.quote: When a browser pane will not render (hidden, throttled), read the page text; structure and copy are often enough for an interaction reference.

units.destination: research.md 'Look, then measure', merged with G1-98.
units.notes: This duplicates the research.md hunk (G1-98).

units.title: App 1: design both sides around one shared record
units.summary: The customer creates the record (a specification), the operator acts on it, and both see the same words for its state.
units.quote: **Design both sides around one shared record.** The customer creates it (a specification), the operator acts on it, and both see the same words for its state.
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md covers one product's UI (states, tables, forms). It has no concept of a customer and an operator surface sharing one record. categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories' covers shared tokens and truth, not shared data.
units.destination: discovery.md §5, with a pointer from app-ui.md §1 Principles (or a short new app-ui.md section on customer/operator products).

units.title: App 2: few meaningful statuses; money tracked apart; derive what can be derived
units.summary: Model the lifecycle with a few meaningful statuses that match real decisions. Track money separately from status. Derive what can be derived (e.g. 'due this week' from the date) instead of making the operator click it.
units.quote: Track money separately from status, and **derive** what can be derived (for example "due this week" from the date) instead of making the operator click it.
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §2 'The state matrix' covers UI component states, not a business-record lifecycle.
units.conflict: 'Status' in 2.0 app-ui.md and anti-patterns.md means UI status indication. Name this 'lifecycle status' to avoid confusion.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 (and the PRODUCT.md Lifecycle section).

units.title: App 3: find the operator's device
units.summary: Owner-operators run their business from a phone. A desktop CRM or CMS admin on a phone is the wrong tool even when it is free.
units.quote: A desktop CRM or CMS admin on a phone is the wrong tool even when it is free.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1: 'For each route write… **device and context** (desk, phone one-handed…)'. categories.md 'Field and frontline tools' and 'Mobile-first consumer'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5. The operator back office is then classified in framing.md like any route (often mobile-first or field-like).

units.title: App 4: CRM, CMS admin, or a custom back office; keep an export path
units.summary: Choose a generic system when the work is generic (contacts, pipelines) and the volume justifies it. Build a small purpose-built back office when the work is domain-specific (a visual spec, capacity, references) and the operator is one person. Keep an export path either way.
units.quote: Build a small purpose-built back office when the work is domain-specific (a visual spec, capacity, references) and the operator is one person. Keep an export path either way.
units.whereInMine: design-systems.md §1 covers choosing component libraries, not choosing business systems.
units.destination: discovery.md §5.

units.title: App 5: honesty is a product feature
units.summary: Estimates come only from the operator's own numbers. Say 'quoted personally' when those numbers are missing. Show policies from settings, not hard-coded copy.
units.quote: Estimates only from the operator's own numbers; "quoted personally" when they are missing; policies shown from settings, not hard-coded copy.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md commitment 2 'Truth is not negotiable'. categories.md Fintech: 'every fee, rate and arrival time before commitment'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5.

units.title: Configurator 1: start from what the customer understands
units.summary: A configurator starts from what the customer understands: a finished example or a shape, not a blank field list.
units.quote: start from what the customer understands (a finished example or a shape)
units.whereInMine: No configurator guidance in 2.0 beyond motion.md §9 ('3D earns its place when… a configurator').
units.destination: discovery.md §5 'Configurators', with a cross-reference from categories.md Ecommerce (product page, variants).

units.title: Configurator 2: one evolving picture of their object; options as pictures
units.summary: Keep one evolving picture of the customer's own object in view, and show each option as a picture of that option.
units.quote: keep one evolving picture of *their* object in view, show options as pictures of that option
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 'Configurators'.

units.title: Configurator 3: group choices into a few chapters
units.summary: Group the configurator's choices into a few chapters rather than one long form.
units.quote: group choices into a few chapters
units.whereInMine: categories.md Public services: 'one thing per page to start with'. ui-ux.md forms rules. None addresses configurator chapters.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 'Configurators'.

units.title: Configurator 4: never lose a choice on going back
units.summary: Going back in the configurator must never lose a choice.
units.quote: never lose a choice on going back
units.whereInMine: app-ui.md §6 Saving: 'warn on navigation with unsaved changes; drafts for long edits'. categories.md Field: 'drafts persist'. accessibility.md: 'never ask for the same information twice in one process'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 'Configurators'.

units.title: Configurator 5: label any generated preview honestly
units.summary: Label any generated preview honestly: a sketch is not a render.
units.quote: label any generated preview honestly (a sketch is not a render)
units.whereInMine: templates/critique.md #24 'Images tell the truth'. motion.md §9: 'Is every fact shown in 3D also in text?'. imagery.md AI-generated imagery rules.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 'Configurators'.

units.title: Write the result in PRODUCT.md, which art direction and architecture then follow
units.summary: Write the §5 outcome in templates/PRODUCT.md: journeys, principles, IA, the configurator model, lifecycle, operator views, and V1 versus later. The art direction and the architecture follow that document.
units.quote: Write the result in `templates/PRODUCT.md`: journeys, principles, IA, the configurator model, lifecycle, operator views, and V1 versus later. That document is what the art direction and the architecture follow.
units.whereInMine: In 2.0, DESIGN.md (brief plus direction) and SYSTEM.md (product UI) are the governing documents. There is no product-definition document.
units.conflict: The documents need an order: PRODUCT.md (what we build) comes first, then the DESIGN.md brief (route categories, top tasks, principles), then SYSTEM.md. The DESIGN.md brief should reference PRODUCT.md rather than restate journeys and principles.
units.destination: discovery.md §5 closing paragraph, plus a line in templates/DESIGN.md Brief ('if PRODUCT.md exists, the brief's surfaces and top tasks come from it').

units.title: Signature experience: treat the differentiating feature as its own product
units.summary: When triage finds a feature meant to be the differentiator (a studio, a configurator, a visualiser, a tool people will play with and show others), treat it as its own product. Six rules follow (G1-47 to G1-52).
units.quote: When the triage finds a feature that is meant to *be* the differentiator (a studio, a configurator, a visualiser, a tool people will play with and show others), treat it as its own product
units.whereInMine: web-design.md intro names an '*experience*' surface mode ('a portfolio or campaign — expressive by design'). motion.md §9 '3D earns its place'. There is nothing on signature product experiences.
units.conflict: 2.0's classification has no posture for a creative tool or configurator that is both expressive and task-driven. Productive rules ('Novelty: near zero', framing.md §2) and ecommerce's 'never in custom checkout controls' would push it toward plain. Add a category row (e.g. 'Signature experience / creative tool') to framing.md §1 and categories.md, or state that these routes are exempt from the productive novelty budget.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b intro, plus a classification row in framing.md §1 and a playbook entry in categories.md.

units.title: Signature 1: write the experiential quality bar first, in the user's words
units.summary: Examples: 'someone opens it and thinks *what is this?*', 'people would screen-record it', 'the output is worth sharing on its own'. Everything after is judged against this bar, not against a feature list.
units.quote: **Write the experiential quality bar first, in the user's words.**
units.whereInMine: DESIGN.md has 'Memory test' and 'Breaks if' (expressive). Neither is a quality bar for an interactive tool.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 1, and possibly a field in PRODUCT.md or DESIGN.md.

units.title: Signature 2: research it as a product
units.summary: Study the best real products doing anything similar, in and outside the category (configurators, creative tools, editors, character creators), and the current technical state of the art. Record what makes their interaction satisfying: direct manipulation, camera behaviour, selection, feedback, constraints, loading, and how they work on phones.
units.quote: Record what makes their *interaction* satisfying: direct manipulation, camera behaviour, selection, feedback, constraints, loading, and how they work on phones.
units.whereInMine: research.md (choose by problem; for product UI, design systems and open-source products). It does not cover creative tools or interaction-feel research.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 2, with a pointer from research.md.

units.title: Signature 3: the architecture follows the experience
units.summary: A signature experience usually needs its own full-screen shell (a dedicated route with its own layout, or a separate app), its own interaction model and its own asset pipeline. It shares the brand (type, colour, motion, tone), not the website's layout. Do not embed it in a page section or an iframe because that is convenient.
units.quote: It shares the brand (type, colour, motion, tone), not the website's layout. Do not embed it in a page section or an iframe because that is convenient.
units.whereInMine: categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories': 'Give each its own type set and density on one token system'. The vocabulary matches 2.0's 'brand layer', but nothing covers a dedicated shell for an experience.
units.conflict: This conflicts with SKILL.md Phase 5 'Keep business logic, routes… exactly as they are' only in greenfield; otherwise it is compatible. The 'shares the brand' wording maps onto 2.0's 'brand layer'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 3.
units.notes: Use 2.0's vocabulary: 'shares the brand layer (type, colour roles, motion tokens, tone)'.

units.title: Signature 4: prove quality with one vertical slice before breadth
units.summary: One excellent instance (one product, one scene, one flow) with real materials, lighting, motion and direct manipulation is the gate. More options come only after the slice passes the bar. Mass-producing weak assets or options is the failure mode.
units.quote: **Prove quality with one vertical slice before breadth.**
units.whereInMine: motion.md §9 gates: 'is there a real asset (a low-poly placeholder is worse than photographs)?'
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 4.

units.title: Signature 5: scale quality with tiers; don't delete it for performance
units.summary: Offer quality tiers (high, standard, low) and fallbacks. Optimise the ambitious version rather than designing a lesser one 'for performance'.
units.quote: Optimise the ambitious version rather than designing a lesser one "for performance".
units.whereInMine: performance.md §1 budgets: marketing 'JavaScript, initial ≤ 100 KB', app '≤ 300 KB'. 'A beautiful redesign that is slower than the site it replaces has failed.' motion.md §9: poster first, load late, frameloop='demand'.
units.conflict: This tension is only apparent: 2.0 treats performance as a hard budget per category, and the branch refuses to downgrade the experience. The reconciliation is to give the signature route its own budget row (it cannot fit the marketing 100 KB), keep poster-first and lazy loading from motion.md §9, and use adaptive tiers rather than a simpler design. Budgets for the pages around it stay as they are.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 5, plus a 'signature experience route' row or note in performance.md §1.
units.notes: The branch's realtime-3d.md (another group) holds the detail on adaptive quality.

units.title: Signature 6: keep it practical
units.summary: The signature experience must also solve the business's real problem: less ambiguity, better specifications, fewer messages. Spectacle that does not improve understanding, confidence, sharing or ordering does not belong.
units.quote: Spectacle that doesn't improve understanding, confidence, sharing or ordering doesn't belong.
units.whereInMine: motion.md §9: '3D is decoration when it is spinning blobs…'. motion.md §1 'What motion is for'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b item 6.

units.title: The trap: a signature experience shrunk to a form with a small preview
units.summary: The failure this section prevents: a builder, configurator or studio that was meant to be why the business is remembered gets reduced to a step-by-step form with a small preview, because it had to fit between two website sections.
units.quote: reduced to "a step-by-step form with a small preview" because it had to fit between two website sections.
units.whereInMine: anti-patterns.md has no entry for this.
units.destination: discovery.md §5b closing paragraph, plus an anti-patterns.md entry (the branch's anti-patterns.md adds 'Shrinking a signature experience to fit the website', inventoried by another group).

units.title: Prototype overtakes original: promote it like a product team
units.summary: A signature experience sometimes gets a second, deliberately different attempt (new visual direction, engine or interaction model), built beside the working one as an experiment and compared honestly. If the user chooses the experiment, it stops being an experiment. Promote it the way a product team would, not a hackathon.
units.quote: Promote it the way a product team would, not the way a hackathon would
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c intro.
units.notes: The lesson row (2026-09-28 The Cake Junction, Cake Studio experiment won) is in the branch's lessons.md, inventoried by another group.

units.title: Promotion 1: preserve the original temporarily
units.summary: Move the original to an unlisted route and keep its code, data shape and tests. Say so in the project memory. It is the fallback until the new version is verified where it matters (real devices, the real order flow), and the reference for behaviour the experiment skipped.
units.quote: **Preserve the original temporarily.** Move it to an unlisted route, keep its code, data shape and tests, and say so in the project memory.
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0.
units.conflict: parity.mjs flags lost routes. An unlisted route still exists, so it is compatible.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 1.

units.title: Promotion 2: inspect first and write the migration as a list
units.summary: Before moving anything, inspect the routes, the design/order data model, save and load, order submission, templates, and every screenshot and sentence on the site that describes the old version. Write the migration as a list before changing a line.
units.quote: Write the migration as a list before changing a line.
units.whereInMine: audit.md §1 preserved-list ('Write the **preserved-list**: routes, anchors…'), which is the analogous discipline for a redesign.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 2.

units.title: Promotion 3: transfer the business functionality, not just the front end
units.summary: The product still needs the structured document behind it (what the business receives), persistence by id, the hand-off into the request or checkout flow, admin views, share links and previews, and tests. A version field on the saved document lets both shapes live in one table while the old one is retired.
units.quote: A version field on the saved document lets both shapes live in one table while the old one is retired.
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md: 'Keep business logic, routes, forms, ids and contracts exactly as they are'. categories.md Ecommerce: 'the contract wins… changes to what the server receives are deploy blockers'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 3.

units.title: Promotion 4: replace outdated marketing material
units.summary: Screenshots, renders, illustrations, copy and CTAs that showed the old version now misrepresent the product. Regenerate them from the new version (real captures, not mock-ups) and audit every page for stale wording.
units.quote: Regenerate them from the new one (real captures, not mock-ups) and audit every page for stale wording.
units.whereInMine: categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories': 'Share the truth: the marketing site shows the product in the product's real tokens'. critique.md #24 'Images tell the truth'.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 4.

units.title: Promotion 5: re-evaluate the surrounding website
units.summary: A signature experience with strong visual personality raises what visitors expect of the pages around it. The site should share its art direction, motion personality and small motifs without turning into the product's UI. It should use its own strengths (real photography, story, trust) to lead people into the experience. Plan that pass explicitly.
units.quote: **Re-evaluate the surrounding website, because the product's quality bar has changed.**
units.whereInMine: categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories': '…recommend a refine of the product so the two meet. Never let marketing type, motion or gradients leak into the app, or app density into the landing page.'
units.conflict: 2.0 prevents leakage from marketing into the app. The branch pulls the product's personality outward into the site. Both agree the site must not become product UI, so they are compatible if phrased as sharing the brand layer.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 5, with a sentence in categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories'.

units.title: Promotion 6: remove the original only after the migration is verified
units.summary: Remove the original only once the new version is integrated, tested on desktop and mobile, and clearly working inside the real product.
units.quote: **Remove the original only after the migration is verified.**
units.whereInMine: Nothing in 2.0.
units.destination: discovery.md §5c item 6.

units.title: Principle: a signature experience changes what the website around it must be
units.summary: A signature product experience changes the visual expectations of the brand website around it. The marketing experience must evolve to represent the product customers actually receive, or the site and the product read as two different companies.
units.quote: a signature product experience changes the visual expectations of the brand website around it.
units.whereInMine: Closest is categories.md 'When a repo holds several categories' ('Share the truth').
units.destination: discovery.md §5c closing paragraph.

units.title: Greenfield 1: write a requirements table before scaffolding
units.summary: Before scaffolding, write a requirements table of what the product needs: static SEO pages, an interactive client, uploads, auth (and for whom), capacity rules, notifications, cost at the business's scale, and who maintains it.
units.quote: Before scaffolding, write a requirements table (what the *product* needs
units.whereInMine: SKILL.md Phase 5 'Stay in the existing framework'. design-systems.md §1 table 'For new product work, when there is nothing to reuse' covers component libraries only.

units.title: Greenfield 2: compare real options, including 'use an existing product'
units.summary: Compare real options, including using an existing product. Record the choice and why each major alternative lost.
units.quote: then compare real options, including "use an existing product". Record the choice and why each major alternative lost.

units.title: SKILL.md section: signature experience or supporting feature?
units.summary: Before designing an interactive feature, classify it. A supporting feature (form, filter, pricing table) stays simple. A signature experience is meant to differentiate the business, delight people, get shared, or become part of the brand. Signals: the user calls it a defining reason for the site, compares it to software people love, or describes a 'wow, what is this?' reaction. Such a feature is never simplified to fit a website section: research it as a product, prototype a vertical slice against a quality bar, and give it its own full-screen route or app. Simplify only where that improves the experience, never for convenience, and never call a mediocre experience 'performance optimisation'.
units.quote: A signature experience is never simplified until it fits a website section.
units.whereInMine: framing.md §1–2 and categories.md: every route is expressive or productive. A productive route gets novelty 'near zero', motion 'only to explain change', and brand only in type, colour roles, tone, empty states and rare moments. motion.md §3: App/SaaS is 'productive everywhere'. There is no category for a creative tool, builder or configurator (rg for editor, builder, creative or configurat in categories.md and framing.md finds nothing).
units.conflict: Under 2.0 framing, a full-screen builder or configurator that people use repeatedly in a session classifies as an app (productive). That sets novelty and expressive motion near zero, which is the 'shrink it to fit' outcome this commitment exists to prevent. The merge needs a category or posture for signature experiences, for example a creative-tool row with expressive interaction and fidelity but productive chrome. Otherwise the framing table overrides the commitment.
units.destination: SKILL.md commitments, a new category row in the framing.md §1 table, and a matching column in the categories.md dials
units.notes: CORRECTION: was 'none'. The rule has no home in 2.0, and 2.0's posture system actively pushes the other way.

units.title: Accumulate while the camera rests
units.summary: When the camera is still, jitter the projection sub-pixel and average frames (and wander the key light for soft shadows), then stop rendering. You get supersampled edges and soft shadows for free, because most of the time the user is looking, not orbiting.

units.title: Procedural SVG must be deterministic between server and browser
units.summary: Sorting generated shapes by floating-point depth can put symmetric twins in a different order in Node and in the browser, which causes a hydration mismatch. Round the values before comparing and add a tiebreak.
units.quote: Procedurally generated SVG must be deterministic between server and browser.
units.whereInMine: multilingual.md 'Say which calendar, in code': 'the same code renders different dates on the server and the client (a hydration mismatch)' (ICU in Node 22 against CLDR in Chromium).
units.destination: visual-qa.md Rendering traps, next to the existing hydration example, or as one general rule that server and client must compute the same output
units.notes: CORRECTION: was 'none'. 2.0 already has the same failure class (server and client disagree, causing a hydration mismatch) for locale data; the branch adds the float-sort case.

units.title: A page that clips itself lies about overflow: inspect element boxes, not scrollWidth
units.summary: `overflow-x: clip` (or `hidden`) on the body, a hero or a section stops a horizontal fault from reaching scrollWidth. A detector comparing scrollWidth with clientWidth then reports 'no overflow' while the render shows copy cut at the viewport edge. Inspect the elements instead: any readable element whose box ends past the viewport is a fault, unless it sits inside a deliberate horizontal scroller or is a single-line ellipsis whose own box fits.
units.quote: A page that clips itself lies about overflow.
units.whereInMine: lib/inventory.mjs clippedText (audit.mjs: 'Text cut off by an overflow:hidden/clip container') catches text cut by a hero or section clip, but its walk stops before body. lib/probes.mjs overflowCulprits only reports when scrollWidth > clientWidth (capture.mjs/audit.mjs print `over.overflow ? … : null`). a11y.mjs checks cut-off content only at 320/640 and only when more than 50% is hidden. visual-qa.md:95: "Stop the walk at `body` (`audit.mjs` does)." visual-qa.md:98: "Text clipped by an `overflow: hidden` card … `audit.mjs` reports it."
units.conflict: visual-qa.md:94 prescribes "Clip the ancestor with `overflow-x: clip`" as the fix for enter-animation overhang. That is the same clip that hides real faults, so the merged text must add: after clipping, check element boxes. A body- or html-level clip is invisible to every 2.0 detector.
units.destination: visual-qa.md > Rendering traps seen repeatedly (merge with the :94-95 and :98 bullets); script side: lib/probes.mjs overflowCulprits should report readable elements whose box passes the viewport even when scrollWidth == clientWidth (exempting auto/scroll scrollers and single-line ellipses that fit), and capture.mjs/audit.mjs should print them
units.notes: Commit 9b040ae (CleoHR prototypes). Lesson row (another group's file): the 390px hero ran 40px past the viewport while the harness said 'no overflow'. The same commit's implementation.md rules belong to another group: minmax(0,1fr), inline-block glyphs, and reduced-motion `transition-delay: 0s !important` (2.0 has no transition-delay rule anywhere).

Write `minmax(0, 1fr)` for every fallback, and give grid or flex children that hold nowrap text `min-width: 0`.
units.quote: `grid-template-columns: 1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`.

units.title: 3D and WebGL: judge only on a real GPU in a focused browser, and log the renderer
units.summary: Embedded preview panes throttle requestAnimationFrame when the window is not focused, and the default headless shell renders WebGL in software (SwiftShader), so neither can judge motion or speed. Capture with full Chromium and GPU flags (on Windows: --use-angle=d3d11 --ignore-gpu-blocklist --enable-gpu), log WEBGL_debug_renderer_info with every capture, and run the e2e project the same way.

units.destination: visual-qa.md (the rule), plus a script feature: a --gpu or --headed launch mode with ANGLE/GPU flags in scripts/lib/env.mjs, and a renderer line in capture.mjs output from WEBGL_debug_renderer_info that warns when it is SwiftShader

units.title: Digest lines for the 20 branch lessons (derived, not in branch)
units.summary: The branch has no digest because it branched before 2.0 added one. Adding 20 rows to 2.0's table without digest bullets would leave the digest stale. 2.0 tells the reader to read only the digest at Phase 3, so these lessons would effectively be skipped. Proposed bullets: (1) assuming a repository and a site to audit when the brief is an Instagram account and an empty folder, and shrinking a signature product to fit the website; (2) two primary buttons in the first viewport, and a phone hero that is only a paragraph; (3) judging WebGL in a software-rendered pane, judging generated geometry by silhouette rather than lighting, and judging costs by intuition rather than experiment flags; (4) moving the canvas under the pointer; (5) trusting a page that clips itself to report its own overflow, plus `1fr` fallbacks, bare-span glyphs and reduced-motion delays; (6) the skill's own massive footer wordmark, and accessibility judged from renders with no axe or keyboard pass; (7) motion built as a generic reveal system instead of a few researched signature moments, and a winning experiment promoted without moving its business behaviour.

units.title: Lesson 2026-09-28 CleoHR website: a page that clips itself hides 40px overflow; `1fr` fallback
units.summary: Project: CleoHR website redesign (two Astro prototypes). The 390px hero on two pages ran 40px past the viewport, and the capture harness reported 'no overflow' for both. The page clips itself (overflow: clip on the body and the hero), so scrollWidth never grew; the fault showed only in the tiled render. Cause: a single-column fallback written as grid-template-columns: 1fr is minmax(auto, 1fr), and a nowrap search prompt inside a flex row set the track's minimum past the viewport. Change: visual-qa.md: the detector must inspect element boxes against the viewport (skipping scrollers and single-line ellipses), because a clipped page lies about scrollWidth. implementation.md: single-column fallbacks are minmax(0, 1fr), and grid or flex children that hold nowrap text get min-width: 0.

Stop the walk at `body` (`audit.mjs` does)'. inventory.mjs clippedText ('Text cut off by an overflow:hidden/clip container' in audit.mjs, text only, stops at body). technical-qa.md: '`min-width: 0` on flex children that must truncate'. No `1fr` → `minmax(0, 1fr)` rule. The 2.0 detector still has the bug: lib/probes.mjs overflowCulprits sets `overflow: by > 0` with `by = doc.scrollWidth - vw` and skips elements under a clipping ancestor. capture.mjs:191 and audit.mjs:221 warn only when `overflow` is true.

An axe pass then found 138 contrast failures: an orange eyebrow tone passed on ivory but not on the alternate chapter one shade darker, and timestamps at 70% opacity sat inside orange bubbles. Root cause: visual QA judged renders only, nothing ran an automated accessibility or keyboard pass, and the skill's own footer habit had no anti-pattern entry. Change: 'Accessibility that the render does not show' in implementation.md; the automated-pass paragraph and three checks in technical-qa.md; 'Massive branding as a flourish' in anti-patterns.md.
units.quote: The user: the light/dark toggle was only in the footer; the drawn product fragments were selectable text; and the skill had put a viewport-wide "CleoHR" wordmark in the footer, which they called "massive branding" and had removed.
units.whereInMine: Automated-pass half is covered in 2.0. audit.mjs runs axe-core (accessibility.md §10). a11y.mjs checks the heading and landmark outline and reflow at 320 and 640. widgets.mjs has a dialog contract. accessibility.md §2 Contrast table covers 'Every text/ground pair actually used, per theme and per chapter, measured on the real ground'. Not covered: the theme switch belongs in the header, and drawn product fragments must be unselectable and hidden from assistive tech. Contradicted: web-design.md §6 'A large wordmark in the footer is a legitimate identity moment.'
units.conflict: web-design.md §6 endorses exactly what the user rejected on sight: 'A large wordmark in the footer is a legitimate identity moment.' That sentence must be removed or inverted. The lockup appears once in the header and once at footer size; identity is carried by the system, not by scale. The branch's anti-pattern should also join 2.0's 'The model's prior (and this skill's house style)' list, because it is the skill's own habit. The row's root cause ('nothing ran an automated accessibility pass') is partly obsolete in 2.0, but the row stays as history.

Rewrite the last cell to name the 2.0 homes: anti-patterns.md (Composition or 'The model's prior') for massive branding, the fix to web-design.md §6, accessibility.md/implementation.md for the header theme switch and unselectable drawn fragments, and the existing audit.mjs/a11y.mjs pass.

units.title: Lesson 2026-09-28 Cake Junction site: hand-over morph from an off-screen thumbnail; generic motion
units.summary: Project: The Cake Junction website around the Cake Studio. The first website → product hand-over morphed a 136 px thumbnail that was usually out of view. The first way back flew the still off-screen because the destination element sat below the fold. The site's motion had been a generic heading rise. Root cause: shared-element continuity was added as a detail instead of designed as the site's signature moment; nobody had decided which few moments the site should have, from what research, at what phone cost. Change: art-direction.md → Motion language, the signature-moments list: one stage per page; the world moves around the photograph; continuity with a landing target; position-mapped storytelling from the product's own parts; a reacting template; the tool order and the phone budget; filmstrips on the GPU.
units.quote: The first website → product hand-over morphed a 136 px thumbnail that was usually out of view, and the first way back flew the still off-screen because the destination element sat below the fold; the site's motion had been a generic heading rise.

Not covered: a landing target for the way back, a still pixel-identical to the first live frame, position-mapped scroll storytelling (≤ ~2.5 screens), a reacting template, the tool order, the phone budget and filmstrip judging.

State it as a signature-site budget, not a replacement. The branch's 'no WebGL on marketing pages' should be reconciled with 2.0's purpose-gated 3D row.

units.title: Lesson 2026-09-28 Cake Studio: a parallel game-like experiment overtook the 3D original
units.summary: After a graphics pass, the 3D Studio was technically good, but the user still felt it lacked visual character. They asked for a parallel, game-like experiment (illustrated art, immediate feedback, a coherent little world) built beside it and compared honestly. The experiment won and became the product. Root cause: the skill knew how to build a signature experience but not how a second, different attempt overtakes the first: what to preserve, how to promote, what business behaviour must move with the front end, and that the surrounding site's marketing and quality bar change with it. Change: discovery.md §5c 'When an experimental prototype overtakes the original' (preserve, promote deliberately, transfer business functionality, replace marketing material, re-evaluate the site, remove only after verification) and the principle that a signature experience raises the website's expectations; pointer in SKILL.md.
units.quote: After a graphics pass, the 3D Studio was technically good but the user still felt it lacked visual character, and asked for a parallel, game-like experiment (illustrated art, immediate feedback, a coherent little world) built beside it and compared honestly. The experiment won and became the product.
units.whereInMine: No coverage. Nearest tooling: parity.mjs ('every old route, id, form field, form submission and data-* analytics' checked against the old build) could verify the 'transfer business functionality / remove only after verification' step. framing.md §2 intensity (a promotion is a rethink of that route).
units.conflict: Vocabulary: the branch cites discovery.md §5c, which has no 2.0 counterpart. In 2.0 terms, promoting the prototype is a 'rethink' of the signature route and should reuse parity.mjs as the verification gate before removal.

units.title: The documented scan matrix is larger than what a11y.mjs actually scans
units.summary: product-ui.md §8 promises a11y.mjs 'clean on every route × theme × phone width with overlays open', and §5 says axe runs 'on every route in both themes'. The script does less. (1) It skips any theme other than the first unless the width is the widest (`if (theme !== themes[0] && width !== Math.max(...widths)) continue`), so dark mode is never scanned at phone width. (2) It presses the --open chord only when `!mobile` (width ≥ 768), so phone overlays such as the Menu drawer are never scanned open. (3) --open is parsed with Object.fromEntries, so each path gets one chord and a second chord for the same path overwrites the first. (4) It does not reload between the base scan and the +open scan. The docs and the script disagree.
units.quote: `scripts/a11y.mjs` clean on every route × theme × phone width with overlays open
units.whereInMine: 2.0 has no theme dimension in any scan: audit.mjs runs axe per path × width at the default colour scheme; only capture.mjs has --dark, and a11y.mjs uses dark only for forced-colours. 2.0 states.mjs can open overlays through steps at any device.
units.conflict: The branch's own text (product-ui.md §5/§8, technical-qa.md, README 'per route × theme × width, overlays opened') promises more than its script does.
units.destination: scripts/audit.mjs (theme loop and open steps, or reuse states.mjs steps) + references/accessibility.md tool notes + technical-qa.md Accessibility
units.notes: When porting P3-03/P3-04/P3-08, either scan dark and --open at phone widths too, or state the reduced matrix honestly in the docs. The phone drawer is the overlay the branch's own traps list (bare phone top bar) cares about.

units.title: How the monospace check detects faces, and its blind spots
units.summary: fontAudit visits every `body *` element (except script/style/noscript/template) that has its own non-empty text node. It takes only the FIRST family of the computed font-family and flags it if that family matches /mono|courier|consolas|menlo|monaco|code/i or equals 'monospace'. It prints up to 6 offenders per view as tag.class "text…" (family), counts views rather than elements (monoViews), and also runs on the +open overlay scans. Blind spots follow from this: input/textarea values and placeholders are never inspected, because form controls have no child text nodes, yet that is exactly where passwords, IDs and [placeholders] live (P2-02). Also missed: ::before/::after content, shadow DOM, iframes, and a mono face that is second in the stack after a web font that failed to load. The regex also gives false positives on display faces such as 'Monoton' or 'Monotype Corsiva'.
units.quote: const MONO = /mono|courier|consolas|menlo|monaco|code/i;
units.whereInMine: scripts/lib/inventory.mjs already records the first computed family of every text element with its character share (`const fam = cs.fontFamily.split(',')[0]…`, families map), and audit.mjs reports 'Families (declared)' and unavailableFamilies. Nothing fails on monospace.
units.destination: scripts/lib/inventory.mjs + scripts/audit.mjs (a fail finding with --allow-mono), plus a tools/regress fixture (a page with a bare <kbd>, a mono input value and a placeholder)
units.notes: The port is small because 2.0 already collects the data. Also check computed fonts of input/textarea/select and their ::placeholder. The inventory is inconsistent here: P1-70 and P4-21 say 'none' while P3-09 says 'partial' for the same check. 'partial' is the right value for all three, because the family data is already collected.

units.title: Evidence found only in commit messages: false contrast failures from scans taken mid-animation
units.summary: Commit a96150b: a live scan of brio3.com at 390 px reported nine contrast failures that were really text caught mid-fade (signal orange at 75% opacity); with animations finished there were none. Commit a6ff89a: zeroing CSS timing was not enough, because scroll-reveal sections stay transparent until they enter the viewport, so anything below the fold on a phone was scanned as invisible. Commit 10e2ff1: a console faded in with element.animate() ignores CSS overrides and read 4.26:1; after document.getAnimations().finish(), two consecutive live scans of six pages at two widths were 12/12 clean. Commit 1814ce6: a raw C:\ path made capture.mjs report puppeteer-core as missing on Windows. None of this appears in a reference or lesson row.
units.quote: reported nine contrast failures that were text caught mid-fade
